topics.title: Place Value and Rounding Whole Numbers
topics.summary: Read, write and compare whole numbers in standard, word and expanded form, and round them to any place.

topics.title: Adding, Subtracting, and Multiplying Whole Numbers
topics.summary: Multi-digit addition and subtraction with regrouping and the standard multiplication algorithm; estimate to check reasonableness.

topics.title: Dividing Whole Numbers
topics.summary: Long division with one- and two-digit divisors; remainders and what they mean in word problems; division as the inverse of multiplication.

topics.title: Powers and Exponents
topics.summary: Write repeated multiplication as a power, name base and exponent, and evaluate whole-number powers (squares, cubes, powers of 10); zero and negative exponents are A1.

topics.title: Order of Operations
topics.summary: Evaluate numerical expressions with grouping symbols, exponents and all four operations in the agreed order, incl. nested parentheses and fraction bars.

topics.title: Factors, Multiples, and Divisibility Rules
topics.summary: List factors and multiples of whole numbers and use divisibility rules for 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 9 and 10 to test for factors quickly.

topics.title: Prime Factorization
topics.summary: Classify numbers as prime or composite and write a prime factorization with a factor tree or repeated division, in exponent form.

topics.title: Greatest Common Factor
topics.summary: Find the GCF of two or three numbers by listing factors or from prime factorizations; use it in grouping problems. GCF of monomials is A1.

topics.title: Least Common Multiple
topics.summary: Find the LCM of two or three numbers by listing multiples or from prime factorizations; apply it to scheduling problems and common denominators.

topics.title: Equivalent Fractions and Simplest Form
topics.summary: Fractions as parts of a whole and as division; generate equivalent fractions and reduce fractions to simplest form using the GCF.

topics.title: Mixed Numbers and Improper Fractions
topics.summary: Convert between mixed numbers and improper fractions and locate both on a number line.

topics.title: Comparing and Ordering Fractions
topics.summary: Compare and order fractions and mixed numbers with a least common denominator, benchmark fractions, or cross products.

topics.title: Adding and Subtracting Fractions
topics.summary: Add and subtract fractions with like and unlike denominators using the least common denominator, and simplify the result.

topics.title: Adding and Subtracting Mixed Numbers
topics.summary: Add and subtract mixed numbers, including regrouping a whole when subtracting; mixed-number word problems.

topics.title: Multiplying Fractions and Mixed Numbers
topics.summary: Multiply fractions, whole numbers and mixed numbers, simplifying before multiplying; find a fraction of a quantity.

topics.title: Dividing Fractions and Mixed Numbers
topics.summary: Find reciprocals and divide fractions and mixed numbers by multiplying by the reciprocal; interpret quotients in word problems.

topics.title: Decimal Place Value, Comparing, and Rounding
topics.summary: Read and write decimals to thousandths and beyond, compare and order them, and round to a given place.

topics.title: Adding and Subtracting Decimals
topics.summary: Line up decimal points to add and subtract decimals, estimate by rounding, and solve money problems.

topics.title: Multiplying Decimals
topics.summary: Multiply decimals by counting decimal places, and multiply or divide by powers of 10 by moving the decimal point.

topics.title: Dividing Decimals
topics.summary: Divide decimals by whole numbers and by decimals (shift the divisor to a whole number), annexing zeros and rounding quotients.

topics.title: Converting Between Fractions and Decimals
topics.summary: Write fractions as terminating or repeating decimals (bar notation) by dividing, and decimals as fractions in simplest form.

topics.title: Ratios
topics.summary: Write ratios as a to b, a:b and a/b; part-to-part vs part-to-whole; equivalent ratios, ratio tables and tape diagrams.

topics.title: Rates and Unit Rates
topics.summary: Find unit rates (incl. with fractions), compare unit prices, and use rates such as speed with distance = rate × time.

topics.title: Solving Proportions
topics.summary: Decide whether two ratios form a proportion and solve a/b = x/d with equivalent ratios or cross products; proportion word problems.

topics.title: Scale Drawings and Maps
topics.summary: Use a scale or scale factor to find actual lengths and distances from maps, blueprints and models, and make scale drawings.

topics.title: Converting Units of Measure
topics.summary: Convert length, weight/mass, capacity and time within the customary and metric systems and between systems with conversion factors.

topics.title: Percents, Fractions, and Decimals
topics.summary: Percent as a rate per 100; convert among percents, fractions and decimals, including percents below 1% and above 100%.

topics.title: Finding a Percent of a Number
topics.summary: Find a percent of a number using fractions, decimals or mental math (10%, 1%, 50%), and estimate percents.

topics.title: Solving Percent Problems
topics.summary: Find the part, the whole, or the percent with the percent proportion part/whole = p/100 or the equation part = percent × whole.

topics.title: Percent of Change
topics.summary: Find percent increase and percent decrease, and the new amount after a given percent change.

topics.title: Discounts, Markups, Sales Tax, and Tips
topics.summary: Apply percents to discounts and sale prices, markups, sales tax, tips and commission, including successive percent changes.

topics.title: Simple Interest
topics.summary: Use I = Prt to find interest, principal, rate or time, and the total balance of a simple-interest loan or account.

topics.title: Integers, Opposites, and Absolute Value
topics.summary: Represent integers on a number line, find opposites, compare and order integers, and find absolute value as distance from 0.

topics.title: Adding Integers
topics.summary: Add integers with a number line, counters (zero pairs) and the same-sign/different-sign rules; additive inverses.

topics.title: Subtracting Integers
topics.summary: Subtract integers by adding the opposite; distance between integers on a number line; temperature and elevation problems.

topics.title: Multiplying and Dividing Integers
topics.summary: Sign rules for products and quotients of integers, powers of negative numbers, and order of operations with integers.

topics.title: Rational Numbers
topics.summary: Define rational numbers; place negative fractions and decimals on the number line and compare, order and take absolute values.

topics.title: Operations with Rational Numbers
topics.summary: Add, subtract, multiply and divide positive and negative fractions and decimals, incl. multi-step expressions with order of operations.

topics.title: The Coordinate Plane
topics.summary: Plot and name points in all four quadrants, name axes, origin and quadrants, reflect points over the axes, and find horizontal/vertical distances.

topics.title: Writing Algebraic Expressions
topics.summary: Use variables for unknown numbers and translate verbal phrases (sum, difference, product, quotient, 'less than') into expressions and back.

topics.title: Evaluating Algebraic Expressions
topics.summary: Substitute values, including negatives and fractions, for variables and evaluate with the order of operations; evaluate formulas.

topics.title: Properties of Operations
topics.summary: Commutative, associative, identity and zero properties of addition and multiplication; use them for mental math and equivalent expressions.

topics.title: The Distributive Property
topics.summary: Use a(b + c) = ab + ac to compute mentally, expand expressions such as -3(x - 4), and factor a common number out of a sum.

topics.title: Combining Like Terms
topics.summary: Identify terms, coefficients and like terms, and simplify expressions by combining like terms, including after distributing.

topics.title: Solving One-Step Addition and Subtraction Equations
topics.summary: Check whether a value is a solution; solve x + a = b and x - a = b with inverse operations, incl. integer and decimal values.

topics.title: Solving One-Step Multiplication and Division Equations
topics.summary: Solve ax = b and x/a = b, incl. fractional coefficients (multiply by the reciprocal); write one-step equations from words.

topics.title: Solving Two-Step Equations
topics.summary: Solve ax + b = c and x/a + b = c by undoing operations in reverse order; write and solve two-step equations for word problems.

topics.title: Writing and Graphing Inequalities
topics.summary: Read and write inequalities with <, >, ≤, ≥; graph solution sets on a number line (open vs closed circle); write inequalities from words.

topics.title: Solving One-Step Inequalities
topics.summary: Solve one-step inequalities with inverse operations, reversing the symbol when multiplying or dividing by a negative; graph and check.

topics.title: Solving Two-Step Inequalities
topics.summary: Solve and graph two-step inequalities such as -3x + 5 ≤ 11, and write and solve two-step inequalities for word problems.

topics.title: Proportional Relationships
topics.summary: Recognize proportional relationships in tables and graphs (a line through the origin), find the constant of proportionality k, and write y = kx.

units.title: Square Roots, Real Numbers, and Scientific Notation

topics.title: Square Roots and Cube Roots
topics.summary: Find square roots of perfect squares (both ± roots) and cube roots of perfect cubes; solve x² = p and x³ = p for simple values.

topics.title: Estimating Square Roots and Irrational Numbers
topics.summary: Estimate square roots between consecutive integers and to tenths, recognize irrational numbers such as √2 and π, and place them on a number line.

topics.title: Scientific Notation
topics.summary: Write large and small numbers in scientific notation and standard form using powers of ten (10⁻ⁿ = 1/10ⁿ); compare numbers in scientific notation.

topics.title: Operations with Scientific Notation
topics.summary: Multiply, divide, add and subtract numbers in scientific notation, renormalize the result, and compare magnitudes in context.

topics.title: Angles and Angle Relationships
topics.summary: Name, measure and classify angles (acute, right, obtuse, straight); use complementary, supplementary, vertical and adjacent angles to find measures.

topics.title: Triangles and the Triangle Angle Sum
topics.summary: Classify triangles by sides and angles, use the 180° angle sum to find missing angles, and find exterior angle measures.

topics.title: Polygons and Quadrilaterals
topics.summary: Name polygons by number of sides, classify quadrilaterals (parallelogram, rectangle, rhombus, square, trapezoid), and use the angle sum (n - 2)·180°.

topics.title: Perimeter and Area of Rectangles
topics.summary: Find the perimeter of polygons and the area of rectangles and squares, and find a missing side from a given perimeter or area.

topics.title: Area of Parallelograms and Triangles
topics.summary: Derive and use A = bh and A = ½bh, identifying base and height (including heights outside the figure).

topics.title: Area of Trapezoids and Composite Figures
topics.summary: Use A = ½(b₁ + b₂)h and find areas of composite figures by adding and subtracting simpler shapes.

topics.title: Circles and Circumference
topics.summary: Parts of a circle (center, radius, diameter), the meaning of π, and C = πd = 2πr; find the radius or diameter from the circumference.

topics.title: Area of Circles
topics.summary: Use A = πr², including semicircles and composite figures with circular parts; give exact (in terms of π) and approximate answers.

topics.title: Volume of Prisms
topics.summary: Name solids and their faces, edges and vertices; volume in cubic units; V = Bh for rectangular and triangular prisms, incl. fractional edges.

topics.title: Volume of Cylinders
topics.summary: Use V = πr²h to find the volume of a cylinder or a missing dimension, and compare volumes of containers.

topics.title: Surface Area of Prisms and Cylinders
topics.summary: Use nets to find the surface area of rectangular and triangular prisms and cylinders (S = 2B + Ph, S = 2πr² + 2πrh).

topics.title: The Pythagorean Theorem
topics.summary: Identify legs and hypotenuse and use a² + b² = c² to find a missing side of a right triangle; Pythagorean triples. The converse is GE.

topics.title: Applications of the Pythagorean Theorem
topics.summary: Solve real-world right-triangle problems (ladders, diagonals) and find the distance between two points on the coordinate plane with a right triangle.

topics.title: Translations and Reflections
topics.summary: Translate and reflect figures on the coordinate plane and describe them with coordinate rules such as (x, y) → (x + 3, y - 2) and (x, -y).

topics.title: Rotations and Dilations
topics.summary: Rotate figures 90°, 180° and 270° about the origin and dilate by a scale factor centered at the origin; congruent vs similar images.

topics.title: Mean, Median, Mode, and Range
topics.summary: Find and interpret the mean, median, mode and range of a data set and choose the measure of center that best describes it.

topics.title: Displaying Data: Dot Plots, Stem-and-Leaf Plots, and Histograms
topics.summary: Make and read dot (line) plots, bar graphs, stem-and-leaf plots, frequency tables and histograms, and describe the shape of the data.

topics.title: Box-and-Whisker Plots
topics.summary: Find quartiles, interquartile range and the five-number summary, make and compare box plots, and find mean absolute deviation.

topics.title: Simple Probability
topics.summary: Outcomes, events and sample space; theoretical probability of a simple event as a fraction, decimal and percent; complements; likelihood from 0 to 1.

topics.title: Experimental Probability and Simulations
topics.summary: Find experimental probability (relative frequency) from trials, compare it with theoretical probability, predict outcomes, and run simple simulations.

topics.title: Compound Events and Sample Spaces
topics.summary: List sample spaces with organized lists, tables and tree diagrams, use the Fundamental Counting Principle, and find probabilities of compound events.

topics.title: Variables and Expressions
topics.summary: Translate multi-operation phrases and real situations into algebraic expressions, name terms, factors and coefficients in context, and evaluate.

topics.title: The Real Number System
topics.summary: Classify numbers as natural, whole, integer, rational or irrational with set notation and Venn diagrams, order real numbers, and test closure.

topics.title: Properties of Real Numbers
topics.summary: Commutative, associative, identity, inverse and distributive properties for all reals; justify each step of a simplification; counterexamples.

topics.title: Simplifying Algebraic Expressions
topics.summary: Simplify expressions with several variables, rational coefficients, negatives and nested grouping symbols by distributing and combining like terms.

topics.title: Solving Multi-Step Equations
topics.summary: Solve linear equations that need distributing, combining like terms, and clearing fractions or decimals.

topics.title: Solving Equations with Variables on Both Sides
topics.summary: Collect variable terms on one side, and recognize identities (all real numbers) and contradictions (no solution).

topics.title: Applications of Linear Equations
topics.summary: Write and solve linear equations for consecutive-integer, perimeter, age, distance-rate-time and similar word problems; judge reasonableness.

topics.title: Solving for a Variable
topics.summary: Solve literal equations and formulas for a stated variable, e.g. A = ½bh for h, or ax + b = c for x.

topics.title: Solving Absolute-Value Equations
topics.summary: Isolate the absolute value, then solve |ax + b| = c as two cases; recognize equations with one or no solution.

topics.title: Rates, Ratios, and Proportions
topics.summary: Solve proportions containing variable expressions, e.g. (x + 2)/5 = x/3, and convert rates and units with dimensional analysis.

topics.title: Applications of Proportions
topics.summary: Use similar figures and indirect measurement to find unknown lengths, and find how a scale factor changes perimeter, area and volume.

topics.title: Precision and Accuracy
topics.summary: Compare the precision and accuracy of measurements, check values against a tolerance (e.g. 50 mm ± 0.5 mm), and report results to a sensible accuracy.

topics.title: Inequalities and Interval Notation
topics.summary: Write inequality solution sets in set-builder and interval notation, graph them, and translate verbal constraints into inequalities.

topics.title: Solving Multi-Step Inequalities
topics.summary: Solve inequalities that need distributing and combining like terms, reversing the symbol for negative multipliers; inequality word problems.

topics.title: Solving Inequalities with Variables on Both Sides
topics.summary: Collect variable terms on one side, and recognize inequalities that are true for all real numbers or for none.

topics.title: Solving Compound Inequalities
topics.summary: Solve and graph 'and' inequalities (intersections, e.g. -2 < 3x + 1 ≤ 7) and 'or' inequalities (unions), and write them in interval notation.

topics.title: Solving Absolute-Value Inequalities
topics.summary: Rewrite |ax + b| < c as an 'and' inequality and |ax + b| > c as an 'or' inequality, solve and graph; special cases with c ≤ 0.

topics.title: Graphing Relationships
topics.summary: Match graphs to verbal descriptions, sketch graphs of situations (increasing, decreasing, constant), and tell continuous graphs from discrete ones.

topics.title: Relations and Functions
topics.summary: Show relations as ordered pairs, tables, mapping diagrams and graphs; find domain and range; decide whether a relation is a function (vertical line test).

topics.title: Writing Functions
topics.summary: Identify independent and dependent variables, write a function rule from a table or situation, and evaluate f(x) in function notation.

topics.title: Graphing Functions
topics.summary: Graph a function from its rule with a table of values, choose a reasonable domain and range for a situation, and read values from the graph.

topics.title: Scatter Plots and Trend Lines
topics.summary: Make scatter plots, describe positive, negative or no correlation, and sketch a trend line by eye to make predictions; equations of fit come in Linear Functions.

topics.title: Arithmetic Sequences
topics.summary: Recognize a common difference, extend the sequence, write explicit (aₙ = a₁ + (n - 1)d) and recursive rules, and find the nth term.

topics.title: Identifying Linear Functions
topics.summary: Recognize linear functions from graphs, tables (constant differences) and equations, and write linear equations in standard form Ax + By = C.

topics.title: Using Intercepts
topics.summary: Find x- and y-intercepts from graphs, tables and equations, interpret them in context, and graph Ax + By = C from its intercepts.

topics.title: Rate of Change and Slope
topics.summary: Find rates of change from tables and graphs, read slope as rise over run, and classify positive, negative, zero and undefined slope.

topics.title: The Slope Formula
topics.summary: Use m = (y₂ - y₁)/(x₂ - x₁) to find slope from two points, a table or an equation, and interpret slope as a rate in context.

topics.title: Direct Variation
topics.summary: Identify direct variation y = kx in equations, tables and graphs, find the constant of variation, and solve direct-variation problems.

topics.title: Slope-Intercept Form
topics.summary: Write and graph y = mx + b from a slope and intercept, a graph, or a context, and rewrite equations in slope-intercept form.

topics.title: Point-Slope Form
topics.summary: Write y - y₁ = m(x - x₁) from a point and slope or two points, and convert among point-slope, slope-intercept and standard forms.

topics.title: Line of Best Fit
topics.summary: Fit a line with residuals or linear regression, judge the fit with the correlation coefficient r, predict, and tell correlation from causation.

topics.title: Slopes of Parallel and Perpendicular Lines
topics.summary: Identify parallel lines (equal slopes) and perpendicular lines (negative-reciprocal slopes), and write their equations through a given point.

topics.title: Transforming Linear Functions
topics.summary: Describe how changing m and b translates, rotates or reflects the graph of the parent function f(x) = x, and write g(x) from a described change.

topics.title: Absolute-Value Functions
topics.summary: Graph f(x) = |x| and translations y = |x - h| + k and find the vertex; general transformations of parent functions are A2.

topics.title: Solving Systems by Graphing
topics.summary: Check whether an ordered pair solves a system and solve a system of two linear equations by graphing; estimate non-integer solutions.

topics.title: Solving Systems by Substitution
topics.summary: Solve a linear system by isolating one variable and substituting into the other equation, choosing the easier variable to isolate.

topics.title: Solving Systems by Elimination
topics.summary: Eliminate a variable by adding or subtracting the equations, multiplying one or both equations first when needed; choose an efficient method.

topics.title: Solving Special Systems
topics.summary: Recognize systems with no solution (parallel lines) or infinitely many (same line), and classify systems as consistent/inconsistent, independent/dependent.

topics.title: Applications of Linear Systems
topics.summary: Model and solve two-variable word problems: mixtures, costs and break-even, interest, and rate problems with wind or current.

topics.title: Graphing Linear Inequalities
topics.summary: Graph y < mx + b and Ax + By ≥ C as half-planes (dashed vs solid boundary, test point), and write an inequality from a graph or a constraint.

topics.title: Solving Systems of Linear Inequalities
topics.summary: Graph a system of linear inequalities, identify and test the solution region, and model real-world constraints.

topics.title: Integer Exponents
topics.summary: Zero and negative exponents: simplify and evaluate expressions such as 2⁻³, (-3)⁻⁴ and x⁻²y⁰, writing results with positive exponents.

topics.title: Multiplication Properties of Exponents
topics.summary: Use the product of powers, power of a power and power of a product properties to simplify monomials, incl. negative exponents and scientific notation.

topics.title: Division Properties of Exponents
topics.summary: Use the quotient of powers and power of a quotient properties to simplify quotients of monomials and of numbers in scientific notation.

topics.title: Rational Exponents
topics.summary: Define b^(1/n) as the nth root and b^(m/n) as (ⁿ√b)ᵐ; evaluate and simplify with the exponent properties. Simplifying radicals is A1.10.1.

topics.title: Polynomials
topics.summary: Identify monomials, binomials and trinomials, find the degree, write in standard form with the leading coefficient, and evaluate polynomials.

topics.title: Adding and Subtracting Polynomials
topics.summary: Add and subtract polynomials horizontally and vertically, distributing the negative sign; polynomials are closed under these operations.

topics.title: Multiplying a Polynomial by a Monomial
topics.summary: Multiply monomials and distribute a monomial over a polynomial, simplifying expressions like 3x²(2x - 5) - x(x² + 4).

topics.title: Multiplying Binomials and Polynomials
topics.summary: Multiply binomials with the distributive property, FOIL or an area model, and multiply a binomial by a trinomial.

topics.title: Special Products of Binomials
topics.summary: Square binomials, (a ± b)² = a² ± 2ab + b², and multiply conjugates, (a + b)(a - b) = a² - b²; use them for mental math.

topics.title: Dividing Polynomials
topics.summary: Divide a polynomial by a monomial and by a binomial with long division, writing any remainder; synthetic division and the remainder theorem are A2.

topics.title: Factoring by GCF
topics.summary: Find the GCF of monomials and factor it out of a polynomial, including a negative or a binomial common factor.

topics.title: Factoring by Grouping
topics.summary: Factor four-term polynomials by grouping pairs with a common factor, including rearranging terms and spotting opposite binomials.

topics.title: Factoring x² + bx + c
topics.summary: Factor trinomials with leading coefficient 1 by finding two numbers whose product is c and whose sum is b; check by multiplying.

topics.title: Factoring ax² + bx + c
topics.summary: Factor trinomials with a ≠ 1 by guess-and-check or the ac (grouping) method, factoring out a GCF or -1 first.

topics.title: Factoring Special Products
topics.summary: Recognize and factor perfect-square trinomials and differences of two squares.

topics.title: Choosing a Factoring Method
topics.summary: Factor polynomials completely by combining methods (GCF first, then special products, trinomials, grouping), incl. higher-degree polynomials.

topics.title: Simplifying Radical Expressions
topics.summary: Use the product and quotient properties of square roots to simplify radicals with numbers and variables by removing perfect-square factors.

topics.title: Adding and Subtracting Radical Expressions
topics.summary: Combine like radicals, simplifying first when needed, e.g. √12 + √27 = 5√3.

topics.title: Multiplying and Dividing Radical Expressions
topics.summary: Multiply radicals, incl. binomials with radicals and conjugates, divide radicals, and rationalize denominators.

topics.title: Solving Radical Equations
topics.summary: Solve square-root equations that become linear after isolating the radical and squaring both sides, and check for extraneous solutions.

topics.title: Identifying Quadratic Functions
topics.summary: Recognize quadratic functions from equations, tables (constant second differences) and graphs; direction of opening, vertex as max/min, domain and range.

topics.title: Characteristics of Quadratic Functions
topics.summary: Find zeros, the axis of symmetry and the vertex from a graph or with x = -b/(2a), and interpret maximum or minimum values in context.

topics.title: Graphing Quadratic Functions
topics.summary: Graph y = ax² + bx + c from its axis of symmetry, vertex, y-intercept and symmetric points; projectile-height applications.

topics.title: Transforming Quadratic Functions
topics.summary: Compare y = ax² + c and vertex form y = a(x - h)² + k with y = x²: stretches, compressions, reflections and translations.

topics.title: Solving Quadratic Equations by Graphing
topics.summary: Solve ax² + bx + c = 0 by graphing the related function and reading its zeros; a quadratic has 0, 1 or 2 real solutions.

topics.title: Solving Quadratic Equations by Factoring
topics.summary: Use the Zero Product Property to solve quadratic and factorable higher-degree equations once they are in standard form; area and number problems.

topics.title: Solving Quadratic Equations by Using Square Roots
topics.summary: Solve ax² + c = 0 and (x - h)² = k by isolating the square and taking ± square roots; exact radical and decimal answers.

topics.title: Completing the Square
topics.summary: Make x² + bx a perfect-square trinomial, solve quadratic equations by completing the square (incl. a ≠ 1), and rewrite a quadratic in vertex form.

topics.title: The Quadratic Formula
topics.summary: Solve any quadratic equation with x = (-b ± √(b² - 4ac))/(2a), simplifying radical answers, and choose an efficient solving method.

topics.title: The Discriminant
topics.summary: Use b² - 4ac to tell whether a quadratic equation has two, one or no real solutions and how many x-intercepts its graph has.

topics.title: Nonlinear Systems
topics.summary: Solve a system of one linear and one quadratic equation by graphing, substitution or elimination; it has 0, 1 or 2 solutions.

topics.title: Geometric Sequences
topics.summary: Identify a common ratio, extend the sequence, and write explicit (aₙ = a₁·rⁿ⁻¹) and recursive rules; compare with arithmetic sequences.

topics.title: Exponential Functions
topics.summary: Evaluate and graph f(x) = a·bˣ, identify the y-intercept, asymptote, domain and range, and recognize exponential data (constant ratios) in tables.

topics.title: Exponential Growth and Decay
topics.summary: Model growth and decay with y = a(1 ± r)ᵗ, compound interest and half-life, and identify the growth or decay factor and rate.

topics.title: Linear, Quadratic, and Exponential Models
topics.summary: Decide whether data fit a linear, quadratic or exponential model from differences, ratios and graphs, then write the model and predict.

topics.title: Comparing Functions
topics.summary: Compare key features and average rates of change of functions given as equations, tables, graphs or descriptions; exponential growth eventually exceeds linear.

topics.title: Inverse Variation
topics.summary: Identify inverse variation xy = k in tables, equations and graphs, write and solve inverse-variation problems, and contrast with direct variation.

topics.title: Simplifying Rational Expressions
topics.summary: Find excluded values and simplify rational expressions by factoring and dividing out common factors, including opposite binomials.

topics.title: Multiplying and Dividing Rational Expressions
topics.summary: Multiply and divide rational expressions by factoring, dividing out common factors, and multiplying by the reciprocal.

topics.title: Adding and Subtracting Rational Expressions
topics.summary: Add and subtract rational expressions with like and unlike denominators using the least common denominator of polynomials.

topics.title: Complex Fractions
topics.summary: Simplify complex fractions by combining the numerator and denominator first or by multiplying through by the LCD.

topics.title: Solving Rational Equations
topics.summary: Solve rational equations by multiplying by the LCD and checking for extraneous solutions; work and rate word problems.

topics.title: Organizing and Displaying Data
topics.summary: Read and make bar, double-bar, line and circle graphs, stem-and-leaf plots and two-way frequency tables, and choose an appropriate display.

topics.title: Frequency and Histograms
topics.summary: Make frequency and cumulative frequency tables and histograms with chosen intervals, and read cumulative frequency.

topics.title: Data Distributions
topics.summary: Choose a measure of center, see how outliers affect it, make box plots (quartiles, IQR), describe shape and spread incl. standard deviation; compare data sets.

topics.title: Misleading Graphs and Statistics
topics.summary: Spot how scales, broken axes, distorted areas, cherry-picked statistics and biased samples mislead; sampling methods and bias.

topics.title: Experimental and Theoretical Probability
topics.summary: Compute experimental and theoretical probabilities, complements and odds; use probability to predict and judge fairness, incl. simulations.

topics.title: Independent and Dependent Events
topics.summary: Find P(A and B) for independent events and for dependent events (without replacement), using lists, tables and tree diagrams.

topics.title: Points, Lines, and Planes
topics.summary: Undefined terms point, line, plane; name lines, segments, rays and planes; collinear and coplanar points; how lines and planes intersect; two points determine a line.

topics.title: Measuring Segments
topics.summary: Ruler Postulate: coordinates on a line and distance |a − b|; betweenness of points; Segment Addition; congruent segments; solve for unknown lengths.

topics.title: Midpoints and Segment Bisectors
topics.summary: Midpoint and segment bisector definitions; midpoint on a number line and the midpoint formula in the coordinate plane; find an endpoint given the midpoint.

topics.title: The Distance Formula
topics.summary: Distance between two points from the Pythagorean theorem: d = √((x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)²); lengths and perimeters of figures in the coordinate plane.

topics.title: Measuring and Classifying Angles
topics.summary: Name angles; Protractor Postulate; acute, right, obtuse and straight angles; angle addition (Betweenness of Rays); congruent angles; angle bisectors.

topics.title: Angle Pair Relationships
topics.summary: Identify adjacent, complementary and supplementary angles, linear pairs and vertical angles; solve for unknown measures. Proving the angle-pair theorems comes in GE.2.8.

topics.title: Polygons and Polyhedra
topics.summary: Polygon vocabulary (sides, vertices, diagonals); name polygons by sides; convex vs. concave; equilateral, equiangular, regular; classify triangles; polyhedra faces, edges, vertices.

topics.title: Inductive Reasoning and Conjectures
topics.summary: Make conjectures from patterns and measurements; test them with counterexamples; why diagrams and measurement alone can mislead, so proof is needed.

topics.title: Conditional Statements
topics.summary: If-then form, hypothesis and conclusion; Euler diagrams; converse, inverse and contrapositive, and which of them share the statement's truth value.

topics.title: Definitions and Biconditional Statements
topics.summary: What makes a good definition; definitions as reversible conditionals; write, split and test 'if and only if' (iff) statements.

topics.title: Deductive Reasoning and Direct Proof
topics.summary: Draw valid conclusions from chains of conditionals (Law of Detachment, Law of Syllogism); the structure of a direct proof from the given to the conclusion.

topics.title: Indirect Proof
topics.summary: Proof by contradiction: assume the conclusion is false, reach a contradiction; how indirect proof relates to the contrapositive.

topics.title: Postulates, Theorems, and Deductive Systems
topics.summary: Undefined terms, definitions, postulates and theorems as a deductive system; Euclid's postulates; the first point–line–plane postulates; famous theorems as examples.

topics.title: Algebraic Properties and Two-Column Proofs
topics.summary: Properties of equality (addition, multiplication, substitution, reflexive, symmetric, transitive) as reasons; two-column proofs with segment and angle addition.

topics.title: Proving Theorems About Angles
topics.summary: Prove and use: complements/supplements of equal angles are equal, linear pairs are supplementary, vertical angles are equal, right angles are equal, perpendiculars form right angles.

topics.title: Congruent Polygons and Corresponding Parts
topics.summary: Congruence correspondences and statements (△ABC ≅ △DEF); identify corresponding sides and angles; included sides and angles.

topics.title: SAS and ASA Congruence
topics.summary: SAS and ASA congruence postulates; decide whether given information proves two triangles congruent; why SSA and AAA do not work.

topics.title: Triangle Congruence Proofs and CPCTC
topics.summary: Write two-column proofs that triangles are congruent, then use corresponding parts of congruent triangles to prove segments or angles equal; overlapping triangles.

topics.title: Isosceles and Equilateral Triangles
topics.summary: Isosceles Triangle Theorem and its converse; equilateral ⇔ equiangular; find sides and angles of isosceles triangles; use these facts in proofs.

topics.title: SSS Congruence
topics.summary: SSS congruence theorem; choosing among SAS, ASA and SSS in proofs.

topics.title: Basic Constructions
topics.summary: Compass and straightedge: copy a segment, copy an angle, bisect an angle, construct the perpendicular bisector (midpoint) of a segment; justify each with congruent triangles.

topics.title: The Exterior Angle Inequality Theorem
topics.summary: Properties of inequality as proof reasons; an exterior angle of a triangle is greater than either remote interior angle. The equality version comes in GE.5.4.

topics.title: Side and Angle Inequalities in a Triangle
topics.summary: The longer side is opposite the larger angle and conversely; order the sides or angles of a triangle; the perpendicular is the shortest segment from a point to a line.

topics.title: The Triangle Inequality Theorem
topics.summary: The sum of any two sides exceeds the third; decide whether three lengths form a triangle; find the possible range of a third side.

topics.title: Inequalities in Two Triangles
topics.summary: Hinge Theorem (SAS Inequality) and its converse: with two pairs of equal sides, compare the third sides or the included angles.

topics.title: The Perpendicular Bisector Theorem
topics.summary: Points symmetric about a line; a point is equidistant from a segment's endpoints iff it lies on the perpendicular bisector; construct a perpendicular through any point.

topics.title: Proving Lines Parallel
topics.summary: Name transversal angle pairs (corresponding, alternate interior/exterior, same-side interior); prove lines parallel from them; construct a parallel through a point.

topics.title: The Parallel Postulate and Angles of Parallel Lines
topics.summary: Parallel Postulate (one parallel through an outside point); parallel lines make corresponding and alternate interior angles equal, same-side interior supplementary; solve for x.

topics.title: The Triangle Angle Sum Theorem
topics.summary: The angles of a triangle sum to 180°; an exterior angle equals the sum of the remote interior angles; corollaries (third angles, acute angles of a right triangle).

topics.title: AAS and HL Congruence
topics.summary: AAS congruence theorem and the HL (Hypotenuse-Leg) theorem for right triangles; choose among all five congruence tests in proofs.

topics.title: Slopes of Parallel and Perpendicular Lines
topics.summary: Identify parallel lines (equal slopes) and perpendicular lines (negative-reciprocal slopes), and write their equations through a given point.

topics.title: Polygon Angle Sums
topics.summary: Interior angle sum (n − 2)·180°, quadrilaterals 360°; each angle of a regular polygon; exterior angle sum 360°; find the number of sides from an angle.

topics.title: Properties of Parallelograms
topics.summary: The quadrilateral family; parallelograms: opposite sides and angles equal, consecutive angles supplementary, diagonals bisect each other; point symmetry.

topics.title: Proving a Quadrilateral Is a Parallelogram
topics.summary: Tests: both pairs of opposite sides equal or parallel, one pair both equal and parallel, diagonals bisect each other, opposite angles equal.

topics.title: Rectangles, Rhombuses, and Squares
topics.summary: Definitions and properties (rectangle diagonals equal; rhombus diagonals perpendicular, bisecting the angles); prove a parallelogram is a rectangle, rhombus or square.

topics.title: Trapezoids and Kites
topics.summary: Trapezoid bases, legs and base angles; isosceles trapezoids have equal base angles and equal diagonals; kites have perpendicular diagonals and one pair of equal opposite angles.

topics.title: The Midsegment Theorem
topics.summary: A triangle's midsegment is parallel to the third side and half as long; a trapezoid's midsegment (median) is parallel to the bases and equals their average.

topics.title: Coordinate Proofs
topics.summary: Place figures conveniently on axes; use distance, midpoint and slope to prove properties and to classify triangles and quadrilaterals given by coordinates.

topics.title: Transformations and Translations
topics.summary: Transformations as one-to-one correspondences; preimage, image and prime notation; translations by a vector and by the rule (x, y) → (x + a, y + b).

topics.title: Reflections
topics.summary: Reflection in a line (the mirror is the perpendicular bisector of each point–image segment); coordinate rules for reflecting in the x-axis, y-axis, y = x and y = −x.

topics.title: Rotations
topics.summary: Center, angle and direction of a rotation; coordinate rules for 90°, 180° and 270° about the origin; a rotation as two reflections in intersecting lines.

topics.title: Isometries and Congruence
topics.summary: Compose transformations; two reflections make a translation or rotation; glide reflections; isometries preserve distance and angle; congruence as a sequence of isometries.

topics.title: Symmetry
topics.summary: Line (reflection) symmetry, rotational symmetry and its order, point symmetry; find all the symmetries of a figure.

topics.title: Area of Rectangles and Squares
topics.summary: Area as a measure: area postulates (congruent figures, additivity), unit squares; area of rectangles and squares; square units and conversions.

topics.title: Area of Triangles
topics.summary: A = ½bh using any side as base, including altitudes outside obtuse triangles; area of right triangles; Heron's formula as an extension.

topics.title: Areas of Parallelograms, Trapezoids, and Kites
topics.summary: A = bh for parallelograms, ½h(b₁ + b₂) for trapezoids, ½d₁d₂ for rhombuses and kites; areas of composite figures by decomposing them.

topics.title: The Pythagorean Theorem: Proof and Applications
topics.summary: Prove the Pythagorean theorem with areas; find a missing side of a right triangle in simplest radical form; applications. The converse comes in GE.10.2.

topics.title: Ratios, Proportions, and Similar Polygons
topics.summary: Properties of proportions (means–extremes, extended ratios); similar polygons have equal angles and proportional sides; scale factor; find missing sides.

topics.title: The Side-Splitter Theorem
topics.summary: Triangle Proportionality (Side-Splitter) Theorem and converse; parallel lines cut transversals proportionally; the Triangle Angle Bisector Theorem.

topics.title: AA Similarity
topics.summary: AA Similarity Theorem; prove triangles similar and find lengths; indirect measurement with shadows and mirrors.

topics.title: SAS and SSS Similarity
topics.summary: SAS and SSS Similarity Theorems; choose among AA, SAS and SSS; write similarity proofs.

topics.title: Dilations
topics.summary: Center and scale factor; enlargements and reductions; (x, y) → (kx, ky); images of lines are parallel; similarity as dilation plus isometry; partition a segment in a given ratio.

topics.title: Perimeters and Areas of Similar Figures
topics.summary: Similar figures with scale factor k have perimeters in ratio k and areas in ratio k²; find an unknown area or scale factor. Volumes come in GE.15.9.

topics.title: Similarity in Right Triangles
topics.summary: The altitude to the hypotenuse forms three similar triangles; geometric mean; leg and altitude geometric-mean relationships to find lengths.

topics.title: The Converse of the Pythagorean Theorem
topics.summary: Converse of the Pythagorean theorem; classify a triangle as acute, right or obtuse from its sides; Pythagorean triples and their multiples.

topics.title: Special Right Triangles
topics.summary: 45°-45°-90° and 30°-60°-90° triangles: side ratios 1 : 1 : √2 and 1 : √3 : 2; find missing sides exactly.

topics.title: The Tangent Ratio
topics.summary: tan A = opposite/adjacent; why the ratio depends only on the angle (similarity); find sides with tan; slope as the tangent of a line's angle of inclination.

topics.title: The Sine and Cosine Ratios
topics.summary: Sine and cosine as ratios to the hypotenuse; SOH CAH TOA; sin θ = cos(90° − θ); sin²θ + cos²θ = 1; find sides with sin and cos.

topics.title: Solving Right Triangles
topics.summary: Inverse ratios (sin⁻¹, cos⁻¹, tan⁻¹) to find acute angles; find all sides and angles of a right triangle; angles of elevation and depression.

topics.title: The Law of Sines
topics.summary: Triangle area ½ab sin C; sine of an obtuse angle; Law of Sines to solve triangles given AAS or ASA. The ambiguous SSA case is left to Precalculus.

topics.title: The Law of Cosines
topics.summary: Law of Cosines to solve triangles given SAS or SSS; cosine of an obtuse angle; the law as a generalization of the Pythagorean theorem.

topics.title: Circles, Radii, and Chords
topics.summary: Circle vocabulary (center, radius, diameter, chord, secant); the perpendicular from the center to a chord bisects it; equal chords are equidistant from the center.

topics.title: Tangents
topics.summary: A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of tangency, and conversely; tangent segments from an outside point are equal; common tangents.

topics.title: Central Angles and Arcs
topics.summary: Central angles; minor arcs, major arcs and semicircles and their measures; Arc Addition; equal central angles, chords and arcs go together.

topics.title: Inscribed Angles
topics.summary: An inscribed angle is half its intercepted arc; angles inscribed in the same arc are equal; an angle inscribed in a semicircle is right; the tangent–chord angle.

topics.title: Secant and Tangent Angles
topics.summary: Angles formed by chords, secants and tangents meeting inside a circle (half the sum of the arcs) or outside it (half the difference).

topics.title: Segment Lengths in Circles
topics.summary: Intersecting chords theorem; secant–secant and secant–tangent segment products (power of a point); solve for segment lengths.

topics.title: Equations of Circles
topics.summary: (x − h)² + (y − k)² = r² from the distance formula; write an equation from center and radius; find center and radius, completing the square when needed.

topics.title: Perpendicular Bisectors and the Circumcenter
topics.summary: The perpendicular bisectors of a triangle's sides meet at the circumcenter, center of the circumscribed circle; construct it; where it lies in acute, right and obtuse triangles.

topics.title: Cyclic Quadrilaterals
topics.summary: A quadrilateral is cyclic iff its opposite angles are supplementary; find angles of inscribed quadrilaterals.

topics.title: Angle Bisectors and the Incenter
topics.summary: Points on an angle bisector are equidistant from its sides; a triangle's angle bisectors meet at the incenter, center of the inscribed circle; construct the incircle.

topics.title: Medians, Altitudes, Centroid, and Orthocenter
topics.summary: A triangle's medians meet at the centroid, which divides each median 2 : 1; the altitudes meet at the orthocenter; locate both, including with coordinates.

topics.title: Ceva's Theorem
topics.summary: Ceva's theorem: cevians from the three vertices are concurrent iff the product of the side ratios is 1; use it to prove concurrence.

topics.title: The Euler Line and Napoleon's Theorem
topics.summary: The circumcenter, centroid and orthocenter are collinear (Euler line); Napoleon's theorem on equilateral triangles built on the sides of any triangle.

topics.title: Regular Polygons
topics.summary: Every regular polygon is cyclic; center, radius, apothem and central angle; inscribed and circumscribed polygons; construct an inscribed square, hexagon and equilateral triangle.

topics.title: Perimeter and Area of Regular Polygons
topics.summary: Find side, apothem and perimeter with special right triangles or trig ratios; area A = ½ap (half the apothem times the perimeter).

topics.title: Circumference and Arc Length
topics.summary: π as the limit of polygon perimeters; C = 2πr = πd; arc length as a fraction of the circumference; the radian as arc length ÷ radius. Radian conversions are Precalculus.

topics.title: Areas of Circles and Sectors
topics.summary: A = πr²; area of a sector as a fraction of the circle; area of a segment of a circle; shaded regions and annuli.

topics.title: Lines and Planes in Space
topics.summary: Ways to determine a plane; two planes meet in a line; skew lines; a line parallel to a plane; parallel planes and their properties.

topics.title: Lines Perpendicular to Planes
topics.summary: A line perpendicular to two intersecting lines of a plane is perpendicular to the plane; distance from a point to a plane; the perpendicular compared with slants.

topics.title: The Theorem of the Three Perpendiculars
topics.summary: Orthogonal projection onto a plane; the theorem of the three perpendiculars and its converse; the angle between a line and a plane.

topics.title: Dihedral Angles and Perpendicular Planes
topics.summary: Dihedral angles and their linear angles; congruent dihedral angles; perpendicular planes and the test for them; the angle between skew lines.

topics.title: Polyhedral Angles
topics.summary: Trihedral and polyhedral angles; each plane angle of a trihedral angle is less than the sum of the other two; plane angles of a convex polyhedral angle total less than 360°.

topics.title: Solids, Nets, and Cross Sections
topics.summary: Classify prisms, pyramids, cylinders, cones and spheres; nets; Euler's formula V − E + F = 2; cross sections of solids; solids of revolution.

topics.title: Prisms and Their Surface Area
topics.summary: Right and oblique prisms, parallelepipeds; rectangular solids and the diagonal √(l² + w² + h²); lateral and total surface area of prisms.

topics.title: Volumes of Prisms and Cavalieri's Principle
topics.summary: Volume postulates; V = lwh and V = Bh for prisms; Cavalieri's principle for oblique prisms; cubic units and composite solids.

topics.title: Pyramids: Surface Area and Volume
topics.summary: Regular pyramids, slant height, lateral and total surface area; V = ⅓Bh; parallel cross sections of a pyramid; frustum of a pyramid.

topics.title: Cylinders: Surface Area and Volume
topics.summary: Right and oblique cylinders; net of a cylinder; lateral area 2πrh and total surface area; V = πr²h.

topics.title: Cones: Surface Area and Volume
topics.summary: Right circular cones and slant height; lateral area πrℓ and total surface area; V = ⅓πr²h; frustum of a cone.

topics.title: Spheres: Surface Area and Volume
topics.summary: Spheres and balls, great circles, cross sections, tangent planes; S = 4πr², V = (4/3)πr³; hemispheres and composite solids.

topics.title: Spherical Zones, Segments, and Sectors
topics.summary: Area of a spherical zone (2πrh); volumes of spherical segments and sectors; deriving the volume of the ball from sectors.

topics.title: Similar Solids
topics.summary: Similar solids with scale factor k have surface areas in ratio k² and volumes in ratio k³; effect of changing one or all dimensions on surface area and volume.

topics.title: Regular Polyhedra and Symmetry in Space
topics.summary: The five regular (Platonic) solids and why there are only five; central, plane and axial symmetry of space figures; the symmetries of the cube.

topics.title: Geometry on a Sphere
topics.summary: Great circles as the 'lines' of a sphere; no parallel lines; spherical triangles have angle sums greater than 180°; distance along a great circle.

topics.title: The Geometries of Lobachevsky and Riemann
topics.summary: Saccheri's quadrilateral and the attempts to prove the Parallel Postulate; hyperbolic and elliptic geometries; triangle angle sums less than or more than 180°.

topics.title: Field Axioms and Algebraic Proof
topics.summary: Real-number field axioms (closure, identity, inverse, commutative, associative, distributive) and two-column proofs of simple properties, incl. order and absolute value.

topics.title: Parent Functions and Their Characteristics
topics.summary: Graphs of linear, quadratic, cubic, absolute value, square root, cube root and reciprocal parents; domain/range in interval notation, intercepts, increasing/decreasing.

topics.title: Translations of Functions
topics.summary: Vertical and horizontal shifts y = f(x − h) + k from graphs, tables and equations; describe a shift and write the shifted rule.

topics.title: Reflections, Stretches, and Compressions
topics.summary: Effects of −f(x), f(−x), a·f(x) and f(bx) on a graph; vertical vs. horizontal stretch and compression factors.

topics.title: Combining Transformations
topics.summary: Graph y = a·f(b(x − h)) + k in the correct order and write the rule for a transformed graph of any parent function.

topics.title: Absolute Value Functions and Their Graphs
topics.summary: Graph y = a|b(x − h)| + k with stretches and reflections (vertex, axis, slopes of the arms), write the rule from a graph, solve absolute value equations graphically.

topics.title: Piecewise-Defined Functions
topics.summary: Evaluate, graph and write piecewise functions from graphs or contexts; absolute value written piecewise; step functions such as the greatest integer function ⌊x⌋.

topics.title: Systems of Linear Equations in Three Variables
topics.summary: Solve 3×3 linear systems by elimination and substitution; interpret no-solution and infinitely-many cases as planes; set up and solve 3-variable word problems.

topics.title: Linear Programming
topics.summary: Write constraints and an objective function, graph the feasible region, and find the maximum or minimum at its vertices.

topics.title: Matrices: Addition, Subtraction, and Scalar Multiplication
topics.summary: Matrix vocabulary (dimensions, entries, equal matrices) and data in matrices; add, subtract and scalar-multiply; solve simple matrix equations.

topics.title: Matrix Multiplication
topics.summary: When a product is defined, row-by-column multiplication, non-commutativity, the identity matrix; applications such as price × quantity totals.

topics.title: Solving Systems with Augmented Matrices
topics.summary: Write a system as an augmented matrix; Gaussian and Gauss–Jordan elimination with row operations to (reduced) row-echelon form; inconsistent and dependent systems.

topics.title: Determinants of 2×2 and 3×3 Matrices
topics.summary: Evaluate 2×2 and 3×3 determinants by the diagonal rule and expansion by minors; basic properties; area of a triangle from its vertices.

topics.title: Cramer's Rule
topics.summary: Solve 2×2 and 3×3 linear systems with determinants; recognize that D = 0 means no unique solution.

topics.title: Inverse Matrices and Matrix Equations
topics.summary: Inverse of a 2×2 matrix by formula (det ≠ 0), larger inverses by row reduction or technology; solve AX = B; singular matrices.

topics.title: Standard, Vertex, and Intercept Forms of Quadratic Functions
topics.summary: Convert among standard, vertex and intercept forms; write a quadratic from its vertex and a point, its x-intercepts and a point, or three points (3×3 system).

topics.title: Quadratic Models and Regression
topics.summary: Model projectile, area and revenue problems with quadratics; find and interpret maxima/minima; fit a quadratic to data by second differences or regression.

topics.title: Imaginary Numbers and Powers of i
topics.summary: Define i = √−1, simplify square roots of negative numbers, compute powers of i, and solve equations like x² = −k.

topics.title: Operations with Complex Numbers
topics.summary: Standard form a + bi; add, subtract and multiply; complex conjugates; divide by multiplying by the conjugate; equality of complex numbers.

topics.title: Solving Quadratic Equations with Complex Solutions
topics.summary: Solve any quadratic over the complex numbers by square roots, completing the square or the quadratic formula; classify roots with the discriminant.

topics.title: Writing Quadratic Equations from Their Roots
topics.summary: Sum and product of the roots (−b/a and c/a); write a quadratic with given real or complex roots; check roots without solving.

topics.title: Quadratic Inequalities
topics.summary: Solve ax² + bx + c > 0 (and ≥, <, ≤) with a sign chart or graph, answer in interval notation; graph y < ax² + bx + c in two variables.

topics.title: Factoring Sums and Differences of Cubes
topics.summary: Factor a³ + b³ and a³ − b³ and combine with GCF, grouping and difference of squares to factor higher-degree polynomials completely.

topics.title: Solving Higher-Degree Equations by Factoring and Substitution
topics.summary: Solve equations in quadratic form by substitution (x⁴ − 5x² + 4 = 0, x − 3√x + 2 = 0) and higher-degree equations needing cubes or grouping.

topics.title: Synthetic Division and Synthetic Substitution
topics.summary: Divide by x − c with synthetic division and write P(x) = (x − c)Q(x) + R; evaluate P(c) by synthetic substitution. Long division is Algebra I.

topics.title: The Remainder and Factor Theorems
topics.summary: P(c) is the remainder on division by x − c; x − c is a factor iff P(c) = 0; use a known zero to factor a polynomial completely.

topics.title: The Rational Root Theorem
topics.summary: List possible rational zeros ±p/q, test them with synthetic division, and find all rational zeros of a polynomial with integer coefficients.

topics.title: The Fundamental Theorem of Algebra
topics.summary: A degree-n polynomial has n complex zeros counting multiplicity; complex and irrational conjugate pairs; find all zeros and write a polynomial from given zeros.

topics.title: Descartes' Rule of Signs and Bounds on Zeros
topics.summary: Predict the possible numbers of positive and negative real zeros from sign changes; use the upper and lower bound theorem to limit the search for zeros.

topics.title: Graphing Polynomial Functions
topics.summary: Sketch polynomial graphs from end behavior (leading term), real zeros and their multiplicity (cross vs. touch) and turning points; transformations of y = x³.

topics.title: Locating and Approximating Real Zeros
topics.summary: Use the location principle (a sign change means a zero between), tables, bisection, linear interpolation or a graphing calculator to approximate irrational zeros.

topics.title: Modeling with Polynomial Functions
topics.summary: Build polynomial models from geometry (open-box volume) and data (finite differences, cubic regression); interpret zeros and turning points in context.

units.title: Rational Exponents, Inverses, and Radical Functions

topics.title: nth Roots and Properties of Rational Exponents
topics.summary: Real nth roots (odd vs. even index, negative radicands, |x| for even roots); simplify variable expressions with rational exponents, e.g. (27x⁶)^(2/3).

topics.title: Simplifying and Operating with nth-Root Radicals
topics.summary: Simplify, add, subtract, multiply and divide radicals of index 3 or more, and rationalize denominators with cube and higher roots; square-root cases are Algebra I.

topics.title: Operations on Functions
topics.summary: Sum, difference, product and quotient of functions (f + g, f − g, fg, f/g) from rules, graphs and tables, with the domain of each.

topics.title: Composition of Functions
topics.summary: Evaluate and form f(g(x)) from rules, tables and graphs; domain of a composite; order matters; decompose a function into simpler ones.

topics.title: Inverse Functions
topics.summary: Find inverses algebraically and graphically (reflection in y = x); one-to-one functions and the horizontal line test; restrict domains; verify by composition.

topics.title: Graphing Square Root and Cube Root Functions
topics.summary: Graph y = a√(x − h) + k and y = a∛(x − h) + k by transformations; domain and range; as inverses of y = x² (x ≥ 0) and y = x³.

topics.title: Solving Equations with nth Roots and Rational Exponents
topics.summary: Isolate and raise to a power to solve equations with square roots, cube roots, two radicals or rational exponents; check for extraneous solutions.

topics.title: Exponential Functions and Their Graphs
topics.summary: Graph f(x) = a·b^(x − h) + k: growth (b > 1) vs. decay (0 < b < 1), horizontal asymptote, domain, range and intercept; transformations.

topics.title: The Natural Base e
topics.summary: e as the limit of (1 + 1/n)ⁿ from compounding more often; graph y = eˣ; continuous growth and continuous compounding A = Peʳᵗ.

topics.title: Logarithms and Their Definition
topics.summary: log_b x = y means bʸ = x; convert between forms, evaluate logs (incl. common log and ln), and find the argument, log or base from the other two.

topics.title: Logarithmic Functions and Their Graphs
topics.summary: y = log_b x as the inverse of y = bˣ: graph, vertical asymptote, domain and range; transformations of log and ln graphs.

topics.title: Properties of Logarithms
topics.summary: Product, quotient and power properties; expand and condense log expressions; the change-of-base formula to evaluate any logarithm.

topics.title: Solving Exponential Equations
topics.summary: Solve by rewriting with a common base or by taking logs of both sides, incl. quadratic-form equations like e²ˣ − 3eˣ + 2 = 0.

topics.title: Solving Logarithmic Equations
topics.summary: Solve by condensing, then converting to exponential form or using the one-to-one property; reject extraneous solutions outside the domain.

topics.title: Exponential and Logarithmic Models
topics.summary: Solve growth/decay, compound-interest (time to double), half-life, Newton's law of cooling and pH problems; fit exponential data by regression.

topics.title: Joint and Combined Variation
topics.summary: Extend direct and inverse variation to joint (y = kxz), combined (y = kx/z²) and power variation y = kxⁿ, incl. non-integer n; write and solve problems.

topics.title: Graphing Reciprocal Functions
topics.summary: Graph y = a/(x − h) + k as a transformation of y = 1/x, incl. rewriting (ax + b)/(cx + d) in that form; vertical and horizontal asymptotes, domain and range.

topics.title: Rational Functions: Asymptotes and Holes
topics.summary: Find the domain, vertical asymptotes, holes (removable discontinuities) and horizontal asymptote of p(x)/q(x) by factoring and comparing degrees.

topics.title: Graphing Rational Functions
topics.summary: Sketch rational graphs from intercepts, asymptotes, holes and the sign of f between key x-values; slant asymptotes are Precalculus.

topics.title: Parabolas with Focus and Directrix
topics.summary: Conics as slices of a double cone; locus definition; write and graph (x − h)² = 4p(y − k) and (y − k)² = 4p(x − h) from vertex, focus, directrix and axis.

topics.title: Ellipses Centered at the Origin
topics.summary: Locus definition; x²/a² + y²/b² = 1 with vertices, co-vertices, foci (c² = a² − b²) and major/minor axes; graph and write equations.

topics.title: Hyperbolas Centered at the Origin
topics.summary: Locus definition; x²/a² − y²/b² = 1 and y²/a² − x²/b² = 1 with vertices, foci (c² = a² + b²), asymptotes and the central box; graph and write equations.

topics.title: Solving Nonlinear Systems of Equations
topics.summary: Solve line–conic and conic–conic systems by substitution or elimination; predict the possible number of intersection points from the graphs.

topics.title: Sequences: Explicit and Recursive Formulas
topics.summary: Generate terms of any sequence from explicit and recursive rules, write rules for non-arithmetic patterns (squares, Fibonacci), and view sequences as functions.

topics.title: Series and Sigma Notation
topics.summary: Write series in Σ notation, expand and evaluate finite sums, and find partial sums; index and limits of summation.

topics.title: Arithmetic Series
topics.summary: Arithmetic means and partial sums Sₙ = n(a₁ + aₙ)/2 = n[2a₁ + (n − 1)d]/2, in and out of Σ notation; nth-term rules are Algebra I.

topics.title: Finite Geometric Series
topics.summary: Geometric means and finite sums Sₙ = a₁(1 − rⁿ)/(1 − r), in and out of Σ notation; annuity-style applications; nth-term rules are Algebra I.

topics.title: Infinite Geometric Series
topics.summary: An infinite geometric series converges iff |r| < 1, with sum a₁/(1 − r); write repeating decimals as fractions; recognize divergence.

topics.title: The Binomial Theorem
topics.summary: Expand (a + b)ⁿ with Pascal's triangle and binomial coefficients C(n, k) = n!/(k!(n − k)!); find a specific term; factorial notation.

topics.title: Permutations
topics.summary: Factorials, P(n, r) = n!/(n − r)!, arrangements with repeated objects and circular arrangements, built on the fundamental counting principle.

topics.title: Combinations
topics.summary: Count unordered selections with C(n, r); decide permutation vs. combination; combine counts with 'and' and 'or'.

topics.title: Probability Using Permutations and Combinations
topics.summary: Sample spaces and events; compute theoretical probabilities by counting favorable and total outcomes with permutations and combinations.

topics.title: Compound Events: Mutually Exclusive and Overlapping
topics.summary: Addition rule P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A and B), mutually exclusive events, complements and Venn diagrams.

topics.title: Conditional Probability and Independence
topics.summary: P(B | A) from two-way tables, tree diagrams and the formula; the multiplication rule; test independence with P(B | A) = P(B).

topics.title: Probability Distributions and Expected Value
topics.summary: Random variables, discrete probability distributions (tables and histograms) and expected value; fair games and insurance-style decisions.

topics.title: Binomial Distributions
topics.summary: Binomial experiments; P(k successes) = C(n, k)pᵏ(1 − p)ⁿ⁻ᵏ; 'at least' and 'at most' probabilities; graphs of binomial distributions.

topics.title: Measures of Spread: Variance and Standard Deviation
topics.summary: Compute and interpret variance and standard deviation (technology for large sets); compare data sets; effects of outliers and of adding or scaling data.

topics.title: The Normal Distribution
topics.summary: Normal curves, the 68–95–99.7 rule, z-scores, and standard normal tables or technology for probabilities and percentiles.

topics.title: Sampling Methods and Study Design
topics.summary: Populations vs. samples; random, stratified, cluster, systematic and convenience samples; sources of bias; surveys, experiments and observational studies.

topics.title: Making Inferences from Samples
topics.summary: Estimate population proportions and means from samples, margin of error ≈ 1/√n, and compare treatments in experiments using simulation.

topics.title: Angles in Standard Position and Coterminal Angles
topics.summary: Angles as rotations in degrees (negative and beyond 360°), standard position, coterminal angles, quadrant of the terminal side; degrees-minutes-seconds.

topics.title: The Six Trigonometric Ratios
topics.summary: Sine, cosine, tangent and the reciprocals cosecant, secant, cotangent of acute angles; reciprocal relationships; exact values of all six for 30°, 45°, 60°.

topics.title: Trigonometric Functions of General Angles
topics.summary: Define the six functions from a point (x, y) on the terminal side; reference angles; signs by quadrant; quadrantal angles; exact values at multiples of 30° and 45°.

topics.title: Increasing, Decreasing, and Concavity
topics.summary: Describe how outputs change with inputs from graphs and tables: increasing/decreasing intervals, relative and absolute extrema, concavity, points of inflection.

topics.title: Average Rate of Change
topics.summary: AROC = (f(b) − f(a))/(b − a) as the slope of a secant line, with units; interpret its sign; compare rates over intervals; estimate a rate at a point.

topics.title: The Difference Quotient
topics.summary: Evaluate f(x + h), then form and simplify (f(x + h) − f(x))/h for polynomial, rational and radical functions (rationalizing as needed).

topics.title: Rates of Change in Linear and Quadratic Functions
topics.summary: Over equal input steps linear functions have constant first differences and quadratics constant second differences; a quadratic's AROC changes at a constant rate.

topics.title: Even and Odd Functions
topics.summary: Test f(−x) = f(x) (y-axis symmetry) and f(−x) = −f(x) (origin symmetry) algebraically and graphically; recognize functions that are neither.

topics.title: Polynomial Functions and Rates of Change
topics.summary: Relate a polynomial's zeros, turning points (at most n − 1), local extrema, concavity and inflection points to where its rate of change changes sign.

topics.title: End Behavior and Limit Notation
topics.summary: Describe end behavior of polynomial and rational functions with lim x→±∞; compare degrees for horizontal asymptotes; find slant asymptotes by long division.

topics.title: Rational Functions Near Vertical Asymptotes and Holes
topics.summary: Use sign analysis and one-sided limit notation to describe behavior near vertical asymptotes and holes; graph complete rational functions incl. slant asymptotes.

topics.title: Polynomial and Rational Inequalities
topics.summary: Solve higher-degree polynomial and rational inequalities with critical numbers and sign charts; interval-notation answers; applications.

topics.title: Equivalent Forms of Polynomial and Rational Expressions
topics.summary: Choose standard, factored, or quotient-plus-remainder form to reveal zeros, intercepts, end behavior or asymptotes; use the Binomial Theorem to expand.

topics.title: Writing Functions from Verbal Descriptions
topics.summary: Translate a geometric or applied description into a function of one variable (area, volume, cost, distance) with a sensible domain; optimize graphically.

topics.title: Selecting and Building Function Models
topics.summary: Choose linear, quadratic, polynomial, rational or piecewise models from context or data; fit by regression; state assumptions and domain limits; interpret predictions.

topics.title: Linear and Exponential Change
topics.summary: Arithmetic sequences and linear functions add a constant over equal input steps; geometric sequences and exponentials multiply by one; logs do the reverse.

topics.title: Rewriting Exponential Expressions
topics.summary: Use exponent rules to show a horizontal shift is a vertical dilation, convert growth rates between time periods (annual ↔ monthly), and rewrite e^(kt) as bᵗ.

topics.title: Exponential Models from Data
topics.summary: Construct y = abˣ from two points or a constant-ratio pattern, fit exponential regression, and interpret a and b in context.

topics.title: Comparing Models with Residuals
topics.summary: Compute residuals and read residual plots to decide whether a linear, quadratic or exponential model fits; judge prediction error.

topics.title: Semi-Log Plots and Linearizing Data
topics.summary: Plot (x, log y) to linearize exponential data and recover y = abˣ from the line; log–log plots for power models.

topics.title: Logarithmic Scales
topics.summary: Use pH, decibel, Richter and other logarithmic scales; compare magnitudes by differences of logs; read log-scaled axes.

topics.title: Exponential and Logarithmic Inequalities
topics.summary: Solve inequalities with exponentials and logarithms using monotonicity (reversing for 0 < b < 1) and domain restrictions.

topics.title: Logistic Functions and Models
topics.summary: Interpret y = c/(1 + ae^(−bx)): carrying capacity, initial value, inflection point; fit and use logistic models (the differential-equation form is Calculus).

topics.title: Periodic Phenomena
topics.summary: Identify periodic behavior in graphs and data; period, cycle, amplitude and midline informally; use periodicity to predict values.

topics.title: Radian Measure, Arc Length, and Sector Area
topics.summary: Define radians; convert degrees ↔ radians; arc length s = rθ and sector area A = ½r²θ; linear and angular speed.

topics.title: The Unit Circle
topics.summary: Define cosine and sine as the coordinates of the point at angle θ (radians) on the unit circle; exact values at multiples of π/6 and π/4; trig functions of real numbers.

topics.title: Properties of the Circular Functions
topics.summary: Domain, range and period of the six functions; even/odd behavior; use periodicity and reference angles to evaluate at any real number.

topics.title: Graphs of Sine and Cosine
topics.summary: Graph y = sin x and y = cos x from the unit circle; key points, period, amplitude and midline; y = a sin bx and y = a cos bx.

topics.title: Sinusoidal Transformations
topics.summary: Graph y = a sin(b(x − h)) + k with amplitude, period, phase shift and midline; write the equation of a sinusoid from its graph.

topics.title: Sinusoidal Models
topics.summary: Build sinusoidal models from data or context (tides, Ferris wheels, daylight, simple harmonic motion) and use them to predict.

topics.title: Graphs of Tangent and Cotangent
topics.summary: Graph y = tan x and y = cot x: period π, vertical asymptotes and zeros; transformations a tan(b(x − h)) + k; tangent as slope of the terminal ray.

topics.title: Graphs of Secant and Cosecant
topics.summary: Graph y = sec x and y = csc x as reciprocals of cosine and sine; asymptotes, local extrema and transformations.

topics.title: Inverse Trigonometric Functions
topics.summary: arcsin, arccos and arctan with restricted domains and ranges; exact and calculator values; graphs of the inverse functions.

topics.title: Compositions with Inverse Trigonometric Functions
topics.summary: Evaluate compositions like sin(arccos x) with right-triangle sketches; rewrite as algebraic expressions; when f(f⁻¹(x)) = x holds.

topics.title: Fundamental Trigonometric Identities
topics.summary: Reciprocal, quotient, Pythagorean, cofunction and even/odd identities; use them to evaluate and simplify trigonometric expressions.

topics.title: Verifying Trigonometric Identities
topics.summary: Prove identities by transforming one side: rewrite in sines and cosines, factor, combine fractions, multiply by conjugates.

topics.title: Solving Basic Trigonometric Equations and Inequalities
topics.summary: Solve equations like 2 sin x = 1 on [0, 2π) and for all solutions using periodicity; solve simple trig inequalities from the unit circle or graph.

topics.title: Solving Trigonometric Equations by Factoring and Identities
topics.summary: Solve quadratic-type trig equations, factor, use identities to get a single function, and handle multiple angles such as sin 3x = ½.

topics.title: Sum and Difference Formulas
topics.summary: Formulas for sin(α ± β), cos(α ± β) and tan(α ± β); exact values such as sin 15°; evaluate, verify identities and solve equations with them.

topics.title: Double-Angle Formulas
topics.summary: sin 2θ, cos 2θ (three forms) and tan 2θ; evaluate, simplify, verify identities and solve equations with them.

topics.title: Power-Reducing and Half-Angle Formulas
topics.summary: Rewrite sin²θ and cos²θ in first powers; half-angle formulas for sine, cosine and tangent with the sign chosen by quadrant.

topics.title: Product-to-Sum and Sum-to-Product Formulas
topics.summary: Convert products of sines and cosines to sums and back; use them to evaluate expressions and solve equations.

topics.title: Linear Combinations of Sine and Cosine
topics.summary: Rewrite a cos x + b sin x as R cos(x − φ) to find amplitude and phase; graph and solve equations of this form.

topics.title: The Ambiguous Case (SSA)
topics.summary: Decide whether SSA data give zero, one or two triangles (height test, sines of supplementary angles), solve each case, and pick a method for any three given parts.

topics.title: Heron's Formula
topics.summary: Find a triangle's area from its three sides with Heron's formula; choose between Heron and ½ab sin C (Geometry); areas of polygons split into triangles.

topics.title: Triangle Applications: Bearings and Navigation
topics.summary: Interpret compass and true bearings; solve navigation, surveying and triangulation problems with right and oblique triangles.

topics.title: Vectors and Their Geometric Representation
topics.summary: Vectors as directed segments: magnitude, direction, equal vectors, scalar multiples, head-to-tail and parallelogram addition, resultants.

topics.title: Vectors in Component Form
topics.summary: Component form ⟨a, b⟩ and i, j notation; magnitude, direction angle and unit vectors; resolve a vector into components; add and scale algebraically.

topics.title: Vector Applications: Forces and Velocities
topics.summary: Resultant force, equilibrium, airplane–wind and boat–current problems using components and the laws of sines and cosines.

topics.title: The Dot Product and the Angle Between Vectors
topics.summary: Compute u·v and use its properties, cos θ = u·v/(|u||v|), and test for orthogonal and parallel vectors.

topics.title: Vector Projections and Work
topics.summary: Find proj_v u and decompose u into components parallel and orthogonal to v; work W = F·d.

topics.title: Polar Coordinates
topics.summary: Plot points (r, θ) incl. negative r and multiple representations of one point; convert points between polar and rectangular coordinates.

topics.title: Converting Equations Between Polar and Rectangular Form
topics.summary: Use x = r cos θ, y = r sin θ, r² = x² + y² and tan θ = y/x to rewrite equations of lines, circles and other curves.

topics.title: Graphs of Polar Equations
topics.summary: Graph circles, roses, limaçons, cardioids, lemniscates and spirals using tables and symmetry tests; read r as a function of θ.

topics.title: Rates of Change in Polar Functions
topics.summary: Relate r increasing/decreasing and positive/negative to distance from the pole; average rate of change of r over a θ-interval; extreme values of r.

topics.title: Complex Numbers in Trigonometric Form
topics.summary: Plot a + bi in the complex plane; modulus and argument; convert between rectangular form and r(cos θ + i sin θ).

topics.title: Multiplying and Dividing Complex Numbers in Trigonometric Form
topics.summary: Multiply by multiplying moduli and adding arguments, divide by dividing moduli and subtracting; geometric meaning as rotation and dilation.

topics.title: De Moivre's Theorem and Powers of Complex Numbers
topics.summary: [r(cos θ + i sin θ)]ⁿ = rⁿ(cos nθ + i sin nθ); compute large powers of complex numbers.

topics.title: nth Roots of Complex Numbers
topics.summary: Find all n nth roots of a complex number, place them evenly on a circle, and solve xⁿ = c, incl. the roots of unity.

topics.title: Parametric Equations
topics.summary: Graph curves from x(t), y(t) with tables and orientation; eliminate the parameter to get a rectangular equation; restricted parameter intervals.

topics.title: Parametric Equations for Planar Motion
topics.summary: Model motion with x(t), y(t) incl. projectiles x = v₀t cos θ, y = h + v₀t sin θ − 16t²; find positions, direction and when or where events happen.

topics.title: Rates of Change for Parametric Functions
topics.summary: Average rates of change of x(t) and y(t), the curve's slope as Δy/Δx over a t-interval, and when the particle moves left, right, up or down.

topics.title: Parametrizing Lines, Circles, and Curves
topics.summary: Write parametric equations for line segments, circles (x = h + r cos t, y = k + r sin t), graphs y = f(x) and implicit curves; control direction and speed.

topics.title: Vector-Valued Functions
topics.summary: Position vector p(t) = ⟨x(t), y(t)⟩; displacement and average velocity vectors; connection to parametric motion.

topics.title: Implicitly Defined Relations
topics.summary: Graph and analyze relations such as x² + y² = 25 or xy = 4 that are not functions; solve for y in pieces; find points where the curve is horizontal or vertical.

topics.title: Ellipses with Center (h, k)
topics.summary: Write and graph (x − h)²/a² + (y − k)²/b² = 1 from its features or general form; foci and eccentricity e = c/a; reflective and orbit applications.

topics.title: Hyperbolas with Center (h, k)
topics.summary: Write and graph translated hyperbolas from their features or general form; asymptotes, foci and eccentricity; applications such as LORAN.

topics.title: Classifying Conics from the General Equation
topics.summary: Identify a circle, ellipse, parabola, hyperbola or degenerate case from Ax² + Cy² + Dx + Ey + F = 0 and complete the square to graph it.

topics.title: Rotation of Axes
topics.summary: Eliminate the xy-term using cot 2θ = (A − C)/B; classify conics by the discriminant B² − 4AC; graph rotated conics.

topics.title: Parametric Equations of Conic Sections
