topics.summary: Parametrize ellipses (x = h + a cos t, y = k + b sin t), hyperbolas (sec t, tan t) and parabolas; convert back with Pythagorean identities.

topics.title: Polar Equations of Conics
topics.summary: Focus–directrix definition with eccentricity e; r = ed/(1 ± e cos θ) or ed/(1 ± e sin θ); identify and graph; orbit applications.

topics.title: Partial Fraction Decomposition
topics.summary: Decompose P(x)/Q(x) with distinct and repeated linear factors and irreducible quadratic factors; set up and solve for the constants.

topics.title: Systems of Nonlinear Inequalities
topics.summary: Graph systems involving quadratic, circular and other nonlinear inequalities; describe the solution region and its corner points.

topics.title: Matrices as Linear Transformations
topics.summary: A 2×2 matrix maps vectors ⟨x, y⟩; matrices for rotations, reflections, dilations and shears; |det A| as the area scale factor.

topics.title: Composition and Inverses of Linear Transformations
topics.summary: Composing transformations = multiplying their matrices (order matters); the inverse matrix undoes a transformation; singular matrices collapse the plane.

topics.title: Transition Matrices and Markov Chains
topics.summary: Model changes between states with a transition matrix; predict future and past states with matrix powers and inverses; steady-state vectors.

topics.title: Mathematical Induction
topics.summary: Prove statements about all positive integers (sum formulas, divisibility, inequalities) with a base case and an inductive step.

topics.title: Summation Formulas and Finite Differences
topics.summary: Use the formulas for Σk, Σk² and Σk³ to evaluate sums; find a polynomial model for a sequence from constant finite differences.

topics.title: The Three-Dimensional Coordinate System
topics.summary: Plot points in xyz-space; distance and midpoint formulas in 3D; the equation of a sphere; traces in the coordinate planes.

topics.title: Vectors in Space
topics.summary: Component form ⟨a, b, c⟩, magnitude, unit vectors, operations and the dot product in three dimensions; parallel and orthogonal vectors.

topics.title: The Cross Product
topics.summary: Compute u × v with a determinant; orthogonality, area of a parallelogram or triangle, and the triple scalar product for volume.

topics.title: Equations of Lines and Planes in Space
topics.summary: Parametric and symmetric equations of lines; the equation of a plane from a point and a normal vector; angle between planes; point-to-plane distance.

topics.title: Introduction to Limits
topics.summary: Why calculus needs limits (speed at an instant from average speeds); meaning of lim f(x) = L and limit notation; limit vs. function value.

topics.title: Estimating Limits from Graphs and Tables
topics.summary: Read two-sided and one-sided limits off graphs and numerical tables; decide when a limit does not exist (jump, unbounded, oscillating).

topics.title: Limit Laws and Direct Substitution
topics.summary: Sum, product, quotient, power and composition limit laws; limits of polynomial, rational, root and piecewise functions by direct substitution.

topics.title: Limits by Algebraic Manipulation
topics.summary: Resolve 0/0 forms by factoring and canceling, rationalizing with conjugates, simplifying complex fractions, and using trig identities.

topics.title: The Squeeze Theorem
topics.summary: Bound a function between two with a common limit; prove lim sin x / x = 1 and lim (1 − cos x)/x = 0 and use them in trig limits.

topics.title: Choosing a Limit Strategy
topics.summary: Mixed practice: pick direct substitution, algebra, squeeze, graph or table for a given limit and connect the graphical, numerical and analytic answers.

topics.title: Types of Discontinuities
topics.summary: Recognize removable (hole), jump and infinite discontinuities on graphs and in formulas, including piecewise and rational functions.

topics.title: Continuity at a Point and over an Interval
topics.summary: Three-part definition of continuity at x = a; one-sided continuity at endpoints; continuity of standard functions on their domains.

topics.title: Removing Discontinuities
topics.summary: Redefine a function at a removable discontinuity (continuous extension) and solve for constants that make a piecewise function continuous.

topics.title: Infinite Limits and Vertical Asymptotes
topics.summary: Limits that grow without bound from the left or right; sign analysis near zeros of a denominator; vertical asymptotes of rational and log/trig functions.

topics.title: Limits at Infinity and Horizontal Asymptotes
topics.summary: Limits as x → ±∞ of rational, radical and exponential functions by comparing degrees/dominant terms; horizontal asymptotes; end behavior models.

topics.title: The Intermediate Value Theorem
topics.summary: State the IVT, check its continuity hypothesis, and use it to justify that a value or root exists on an interval.

topics.title: Average and Instantaneous Rates of Change
topics.summary: Secant-line slope as average rate of change; the difference quotient; instantaneous rate as the limit of secant slopes (tangent slope).

topics.title: The Derivative at a Point
topics.summary: Limit definition of f′(a) in both forms; equation of the tangent (and normal) line at a point; recognizing a limit as a derivative.

topics.title: The Derivative as a Function
topics.summary: Find f′(x) from the limit definition; notations f′, y′, dy/dx, d/dx; sketch the graph of f′ from the graph of f.

topics.title: Estimating Derivatives from Tables and Graphs
topics.summary: Approximate f′(a) from data tables and graphs with difference quotients (incl. symmetric); use a calculator's numerical derivative.

topics.title: Differentiability and Continuity
topics.summary: Where a derivative fails (corners, cusps, vertical tangents, discontinuities); differentiable implies continuous; differentiability of piecewise functions.

topics.title: The Power Rule and Basic Derivative Rules
topics.summary: Constant, power (any real exponent), constant-multiple, sum and difference rules; rewriting radicals and reciprocals as powers before differentiating.

topics.title: Derivatives of sin x, cos x, eˣ and ln x
topics.summary: Derivatives of sine, cosine, the natural exponential and the natural log, and their use with the basic rules; other bases come in CA.3.2.

topics.title: The Product Rule
topics.summary: Differentiate products (fg)′ = f′g + fg′, including from tables of values and with trig, exponential and log factors.

topics.title: The Quotient Rule
topics.summary: Differentiate quotients (f/g)′ = (f′g − fg′)/g², including from tables; decide when rewriting beats the quotient rule.

topics.title: Derivatives of tan x, cot x, sec x and csc x
topics.summary: Derive and use the derivatives of the other four trig functions with the quotient rule.

topics.title: The Chain Rule
topics.summary: Differentiate compositions f(g(x)) in both notations, including nested chains, powers of functions, and values from tables and graphs.

topics.title: Derivatives of aˣ and logₐ x
topics.summary: Derivatives of exponential and logarithmic functions with any base, and of e^u and ln u via the chain rule; logarithmic differentiation is CA.11.2.

topics.title: Implicit Differentiation
topics.summary: Differentiate both sides of an equation in x and y with respect to x and solve for dy/dx; slopes and tangent lines of implicit curves.

topics.title: Derivatives of Inverse Functions
topics.summary: Use (f⁻¹)′(a) = 1/f′(f⁻¹(a)) with formulas, tables and graphs; the reciprocal-slope relationship of inverse functions.

topics.title: Derivatives of Inverse Trigonometric Functions
topics.summary: Derivatives of arcsin, arccos, arctan (and arccot, arcsec, arccsc) and their compositions via the chain rule.

topics.title: Choosing a Differentiation Strategy
topics.summary: Mixed practice: decide which rules apply and in what order (rewrite, product, quotient, chain, implicit, inverse) for any given function.

topics.title: Higher-Order Derivatives
topics.summary: Second and higher derivatives and their notation, including second derivatives of implicitly defined relations.

topics.title: Interpreting the Derivative in Context
topics.summary: State the meaning of f′(a) with units in applied settings (marginal cost, population, temperature); rates in science and economics; motion is CA.4.2.

topics.title: Straight-Line Motion: Position, Velocity and Acceleration
topics.summary: v = s′, a = v′ = s″; speed; when a particle moves left/right, is at rest, changes direction, or speeds up/slows down.

topics.title: Introduction to Related Rates
topics.summary: Differentiate an equation relating quantities with respect to time and interpret the related rates; implicit differentiation in t.

topics.title: Solving Related Rates Problems
topics.summary: Full related-rates problems: sketch, relate variables (Pythagorean, similar triangles, volume, trig), differentiate, substitute the instant's values.

topics.title: Local Linearity and Linearization
topics.summary: Tangent-line approximation L(x) = f(a) + f′(a)(x − a); estimate values; use concavity to tell over- vs. underestimates.

topics.title: L'Hôpital's Rule
topics.summary: Evaluate limits of 0/0 and ∞/∞ forms with L'Hôpital's Rule, checking the hypotheses; other indeterminate forms are CA.11.6.

topics.title: The Mean Value Theorem
topics.summary: State and apply the MVT and Rolle's Theorem, verifying hypotheses; find c; consequences (f′ = 0 ⇒ f constant).

topics.title: Extreme Values and Critical Points
topics.summary: Extreme Value Theorem; absolute vs. relative extrema; critical points where f′ = 0 or f′ is undefined.

topics.title: Increasing and Decreasing Functions
topics.summary: Use the sign of f′ (sign chart) to find intervals of increase and decrease, with written justification.

topics.title: The First Derivative Test
topics.summary: Classify critical points as relative maxima, minima or neither from sign changes of f′.

topics.title: The Candidates Test for Absolute Extrema
topics.summary: Find absolute extrema on a closed interval by checking critical points and endpoints (closed interval method).

topics.title: Concavity and Points of Inflection
topics.summary: Concave up/down from the sign of f″ (or f′ increasing/decreasing); find and justify points of inflection.

topics.title: The Second Derivative Test
topics.summary: Classify critical points with f″; when the test is inconclusive and the first derivative test is needed.

topics.title: Sketching Graphs of Functions and Their Derivatives
topics.summary: Sketch f from information about f′ and f″ (and f′ from f); full curve sketching with intercepts, asymptotes, extrema, concavity.

topics.title: Connecting f, f′ and f″
topics.summary: Read and justify the behavior of f from a given graph or table of f′ or f″; match graphs of f, f′, f″.

topics.title: Optimization Problems
topics.summary: Model a quantity to maximize or minimize (area, volume, cost, distance, profit), reduce to one variable, find and justify the absolute extremum.

topics.title: Behaviors of Implicit Relations
topics.summary: Horizontal and vertical tangents, extrema and concavity for implicitly defined curves using dy/dx and d²y/dx².

topics.title: Accumulation of Change
topics.summary: Area under a rate graph as accumulated (net) change; distance from a velocity graph; units of the area; signed area.

topics.title: Riemann Sums: Left, Right and Midpoint
topics.summary: Approximate area with left, right and midpoint rectangles from formulas, graphs and tables (incl. unequal widths); over/under estimates.

topics.title: The Trapezoidal Rule
topics.summary: Approximate a definite integral with trapezoidal sums from formulas and tables; compare with Riemann sums; over/under via concavity.

topics.title: Riemann Sums, Summation Notation and the Definite Integral
topics.summary: Sigma notation; the definite integral as the limit of Riemann sums; converting between a limit of sums and integral notation.

topics.title: Properties of Definite Integrals

topics.title: Writing Functions
topics.summary: Identify independent and dependent variables, write a function rule from a table or situation, and evaluate f(x) in function notation.

topics.title: Graphing Functions
topics.summary: Graph a function from its rule with a table of values, choose a reasonable domain and range for a situation, and read values from the graph.

topics.title: Identifying Linear Functions
topics.summary: Recognize linear functions from graphs, tables (constant differences) and equations, and write linear equations in standard form Ax + By = C.

topics.title: Using Intercepts
topics.summary: Find x- and y-intercepts from graphs, tables and equations, interpret them in context, and graph Ax + By = C from its intercepts.

topics.title: Rate of Change and Slope
topics.summary: Find rates of change from tables and graphs, read slope as rise over run, and classify positive, negative, zero and undefined slope.

topics.title: The Slope Formula
topics.summary: Use m = (y₂ - y₁)/(x₂ - x₁) to find slope from two points, a table or an equation, and interpret slope as a rate in context.

topics.title: Slope-Intercept Form
topics.summary: Write and graph y = mx + b from a slope and intercept, a graph, or a context, and rewrite equations in slope-intercept form.

topics.title: Direct Variation
topics.summary: Identify direct variation y = kx in equations, tables and graphs, find the constant of variation, and solve direct-variation problems.

topics.title: Transforming Linear Functions
topics.summary: Describe how changing m and b translates, rotates or reflects the graph of the parent function f(x) = x, and write g(x) from a described change.

topics.title: Point-Slope Form
topics.summary: Write y - y₁ = m(x - x₁) from a point and slope or two points, and convert among point-slope, slope-intercept and standard forms.

topics.title: Slopes of Parallel and Perpendicular Lines
topics.summary: Identify parallel lines (equal slopes) and perpendicular lines (negative-reciprocal slopes), and write their equations through a given point.

units.title: Systems of Two Linear Equations in Two Variables

topics.title: Solving Systems by Graphing
topics.summary: Check whether an ordered pair solves a system and solve a system of two linear equations by graphing; estimate non-integer solutions.

topics.title: Solving Systems by Substitution
topics.summary: Solve a linear system by isolating one variable and substituting into the other equation, choosing the easier variable to isolate.

topics.title: Solving Systems by Elimination
topics.summary: Eliminate a variable by adding or subtracting the equations, multiplying one or both equations first when needed; choose an efficient method.

topics.title: Solving Special Systems
topics.summary: Recognize systems with no solution (parallel lines) or infinitely many (same line), and classify systems as consistent/inconsistent, independent/dependent.

topics.title: Applications of Linear Systems
topics.summary: Model and solve two-variable word problems: mixtures, costs and break-even, interest, and rate problems with wind or current.

units.title: Linear Inequalities in One or Two Variables

topics.title: Inequalities and Interval Notation
topics.summary: Write inequality solution sets in set-builder and interval notation, graph them, and translate verbal constraints into inequalities.

topics.title: Solving Multi-Step Inequalities
topics.summary: Solve inequalities that need distributing and combining like terms, reversing the symbol for negative multipliers; inequality word problems.

topics.title: Solving Inequalities with Variables on Both Sides
topics.summary: Collect variable terms on one side, and recognize inequalities that are true for all real numbers or for none.

topics.title: Solving Compound Inequalities
topics.summary: Solve and graph 'and' inequalities (intersections, e.g. -2 < 3x + 1 ≤ 7) and 'or' inequalities (unions), and write them in interval notation.

topics.title: Graphing Linear Inequalities
topics.summary: Graph y < mx + b and Ax + By ≥ C as half-planes (dashed vs solid boundary, test point), and write an inequality from a graph or a constraint.

topics.title: Solving Systems of Linear Inequalities
topics.summary: Graph a system of linear inequalities, identify and test the solution region, and model real-world constraints.

topics.title: Integer Exponents
topics.summary: Zero and negative exponents: simplify and evaluate expressions such as 2⁻³, (-3)⁻⁴ and x⁻²y⁰, writing results with positive exponents.

topics.title: Multiplication Properties of Exponents
topics.summary: Use the product of powers, power of a power and power of a product properties to simplify monomials, incl. negative exponents and scientific notation.

topics.title: Division Properties of Exponents
topics.summary: Use the quotient of powers and power of a quotient properties to simplify quotients of monomials and of numbers in scientific notation.

topics.title: Rational Exponents
topics.summary: Define b^(1/n) as the nth root and b^(m/n) as (ⁿ√b)ᵐ; evaluate and simplify with the exponent properties. Simplifying radicals is A1.10.1.

topics.title: nth Roots and Properties of Rational Exponents
topics.summary: Real nth roots (odd vs. even index, negative radicands, |x| for even roots); simplify variable expressions with rational exponents, e.g. (27x⁶)^(2/3).

topics.title: Simplifying Radical Expressions
topics.summary: Use the product and quotient properties of square roots to simplify radicals with numbers and variables by removing perfect-square factors.

units.title: Equivalent Expressions: Polynomial and Rational Expressions

topics.title: Adding and Subtracting Polynomials
topics.summary: Add and subtract polynomials horizontally and vertically, distributing the negative sign; polynomials are closed under these operations.

topics.title: Multiplying Binomials and Polynomials
topics.summary: Multiply binomials with the distributive property, FOIL or an area model, and multiply a binomial by a trinomial.

topics.title: Special Products of Binomials
topics.summary: Square binomials, (a ± b)² = a² ± 2ab + b², and multiply conjugates, (a + b)(a - b) = a² - b²; use them for mental math.

topics.title: Factoring by GCF
topics.summary: Find the GCF of monomials and factor it out of a polynomial, including a negative or a binomial common factor.

topics.title: Factoring x² + bx + c
topics.summary: Factor trinomials with leading coefficient 1 by finding two numbers whose product is c and whose sum is b; check by multiplying.

topics.title: Factoring ax² + bx + c
topics.summary: Factor trinomials with a ≠ 1 by guess-and-check or the ac (grouping) method, factoring out a GCF or -1 first.

topics.title: Factoring Special Products
topics.summary: Recognize and factor perfect-square trinomials and differences of two squares.

topics.title: Simplifying Rational Expressions
topics.summary: Find excluded values and simplify rational expressions by factoring and dividing out common factors, including opposite binomials.

topics.title: Adding and Subtracting Rational Expressions
topics.summary: Add and subtract rational expressions with like and unlike denominators using the least common denominator of polynomials.

topics.title: Dividing Polynomials
topics.summary: Divide a polynomial by a monomial and by a binomial with long division, writing any remainder; synthetic division and the remainder theorem are A2.

topics.title: Characteristics of Quadratic Functions
topics.summary: Find zeros, the axis of symmetry and the vertex from a graph or with x = -b/(2a), and interpret maximum or minimum values in context.

topics.title: Graphing Quadratic Functions
topics.summary: Graph y = ax² + bx + c from its axis of symmetry, vertex, y-intercept and symmetric points; projectile-height applications.

topics.title: Transforming Quadratic Functions
topics.summary: Compare y = ax² + c and vertex form y = a(x - h)² + k with y = x²: stretches, compressions, reflections and translations.

topics.title: Standard, Vertex, and Intercept Forms of Quadratic Functions
topics.summary: Convert among standard, vertex and intercept forms; write a quadratic from its vertex and a point, its x-intercepts and a point, or three points (3×3 system).

topics.title: Exponential Functions
topics.summary: Evaluate and graph f(x) = a·bˣ, identify the y-intercept, asymptote, domain and range, and recognize exponential data (constant ratios) in tables.

topics.title: Exponential Growth and Decay
topics.summary: Model growth and decay with y = a(1 ± r)ᵗ, compound interest and half-life, and identify the growth or decay factor and rate.

topics.title: Translations of Functions
topics.summary: Vertical and horizontal shifts y = f(x − h) + k from graphs, tables and equations; describe a shift and write the shifted rule.

topics.title: Reflections, Stretches, and Compressions
topics.summary: Effects of −f(x), f(−x), a·f(x) and f(bx) on a graph; vertical vs. horizontal stretch and compression factors.

topics.title: The Remainder and Factor Theorems
topics.summary: P(c) is the remainder on division by x − c; x − c is a factor iff P(c) = 0; use a known zero to factor a polynomial completely.

topics.title: Graphing Polynomial Functions
topics.summary: Sketch polynomial graphs from end behavior (leading term), real zeros and their multiplicity (cross vs. touch) and turning points; transformations of y = x³.

topics.title: Composition of Functions
topics.summary: Evaluate and form f(g(x)) from rules, tables and graphs; domain of a composite; order matters; decompose a function into simpler ones.

units.title: Nonlinear Equations in One Variable and Systems in Two Variables

topics.title: Solving Quadratic Equations by Factoring
topics.summary: Use the Zero Product Property to solve quadratic and factorable higher-degree equations once they are in standard form; area and number problems.

topics.title: Solving Quadratic Equations by Using Square Roots
topics.summary: Solve ax² + c = 0 and (x - h)² = k by isolating the square and taking ± square roots; exact radical and decimal answers.

topics.title: Completing the Square
topics.summary: Make x² + bx a perfect-square trinomial, solve quadratic equations by completing the square (incl. a ≠ 1), and rewrite a quadratic in vertex form.

topics.title: The Quadratic Formula
topics.summary: Solve any quadratic equation with x = (-b ± √(b² - 4ac))/(2a), simplifying radical answers, and choose an efficient solving method.

topics.title: The Discriminant
topics.summary: Use b² - 4ac to tell whether a quadratic equation has two, one or no real solutions and how many x-intercepts its graph has.

topics.title: Writing Quadratic Equations from Their Roots
topics.summary: Sum and product of the roots (−b/a and c/a); write a quadratic with given real or complex roots; check roots without solving.

topics.title: Solving Radical Equations
topics.summary: Solve square-root equations that become linear after isolating the radical and squaring both sides, and check for extraneous solutions.

topics.title: Solving Rational Equations
topics.summary: Solve rational equations by multiplying by the LCD and checking for extraneous solutions; work and rate word problems.

topics.title: Solving Absolute-Value Equations
topics.summary: Isolate the absolute value, then solve |ax + b| = c as two cases; recognize equations with one or no solution.

topics.title: Nonlinear Systems
topics.summary: Solve a system of one linear and one quadratic equation by graphing, substitution or elimination; it has 0, 1 or 2 solutions.

topics.title: Scatter Plots and Trend Lines
topics.summary: Make scatter plots, describe positive, negative or no correlation, and sketch a trend line by eye to make predictions; equations of fit come in Linear Functions.

topics.title: Line of Best Fit
topics.summary: Fit a line with residuals or linear regression, judge the fit with the correlation coefficient r, predict, and tell correlation from causation.

topics.title: Linear, Quadratic, and Exponential Models
topics.summary: Decide whether data fit a linear, quadratic or exponential model from differences, ratios and graphs, then write the model and predict.

topics.title: Angle Pair Relationships
topics.summary: Identify adjacent, complementary and supplementary angles, linear pairs and vertical angles; solve for unknown measures. Proving the angle-pair theorems comes in GE.2.8.

topics.title: The Parallel Postulate and Angles of Parallel Lines
topics.summary: Parallel Postulate (one parallel through an outside point); parallel lines make corresponding and alternate interior angles equal, same-side interior supplementary; solve for x.

topics.title: The Triangle Angle Sum Theorem
topics.summary: The angles of a triangle sum to 180°; an exterior angle equals the sum of the remote interior angles; corollaries (third angles, acute angles of a right triangle).

topics.title: Polygon Angle Sums
topics.summary: Interior angle sum (n − 2)·180°, quadrilaterals 360°; each angle of a regular polygon; exterior angle sum 360°; find the number of sides from an angle.

topics.title: Isosceles and Equilateral Triangles
topics.summary: Isosceles Triangle Theorem and its converse; equilateral ⇔ equiangular; find sides and angles of isosceles triangles; use these facts in proofs.

topics.title: SAS and ASA Congruence
topics.summary: SAS and ASA congruence postulates; decide whether given information proves two triangles congruent; why SSA and AAA do not work.

topics.title: Area of Triangles
topics.summary: A = ½bh using any side as base, including altitudes outside obtuse triangles; area of right triangles; Heron's formula as an extension.

topics.title: Ratios, Proportions, and Similar Polygons
topics.summary: Properties of proportions (means–extremes, extended ratios); similar polygons have equal angles and proportional sides; scale factor; find missing sides.

topics.title: The Side-Splitter Theorem
topics.summary: Triangle Proportionality (Side-Splitter) Theorem and converse; parallel lines cut transversals proportionally; the Triangle Angle Bisector Theorem.

topics.title: AA Similarity
topics.summary: AA Similarity Theorem; prove triangles similar and find lengths; indirect measurement with shadows and mirrors.

topics.title: The Pythagorean Theorem
topics.summary: Identify legs and hypotenuse and use a² + b² = c² to find a missing side of a right triangle; Pythagorean triples. The converse is GE.

topics.title: The Converse of the Pythagorean Theorem
topics.summary: Converse of the Pythagorean theorem; classify a triangle as acute, right or obtuse from its sides; Pythagorean triples and their multiples.

topics.title: Special Right Triangles
topics.summary: 45°-45°-90° and 30°-60°-90° triangles: side ratios 1 : 1 : √2 and 1 : √3 : 2; find missing sides exactly.

topics.title: The Distance Formula
topics.summary: Distance between two points from the Pythagorean theorem: d = √((x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)²); lengths and perimeters of figures in the coordinate plane.

topics.title: The Tangent Ratio
topics.summary: tan A = opposite/adjacent; why the ratio depends only on the angle (similarity); find sides with tan; slope as the tangent of a line's angle of inclination.

topics.title: The Sine and Cosine Ratios
topics.summary: Sine and cosine as ratios to the hypotenuse; SOH CAH TOA; sin θ = cos(90° − θ); sin²θ + cos²θ = 1; find sides with sin and cos.

topics.title: Solving Right Triangles
topics.summary: Inverse ratios (sin⁻¹, cos⁻¹, tan⁻¹) to find acute angles; find all sides and angles of a right triangle; angles of elevation and depression.

topics.title: Circles, Radii, and Chords
topics.summary: Circle vocabulary (center, radius, diameter, chord, secant); the perpendicular from the center to a chord bisects it; equal chords are equidistant from the center.

topics.title: Tangents
topics.summary: A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of tangency, and conversely; tangent segments from an outside point are equal; common tangents.

topics.title: Central Angles and Arcs
topics.summary: Central angles; minor arcs, major arcs and semicircles and their measures; Arc Addition; equal central angles, chords and arcs go together.

topics.title: Inscribed Angles
topics.summary: An inscribed angle is half its intercepted arc; angles inscribed in the same arc are equal; an angle inscribed in a semicircle is right; the tangent–chord angle.

topics.title: Circumference and Arc Length
topics.summary: π as the limit of polygon perimeters; C = 2πr = πd; arc length as a fraction of the circumference; the radian as arc length ÷ radius. Radian conversions are Precalculus.

topics.title: Areas of Circles and Sectors
topics.summary: A = πr²; area of a sector as a fraction of the circle; area of a segment of a circle; shaded regions and annuli.

topics.title: Radian Measure, Arc Length, and Sector Area
topics.summary: Define radians; convert degrees ↔ radians; arc length s = rθ and sector area A = ½r²θ; linear and angular speed.

topics.title: The Unit Circle
topics.summary: Define cosine and sine as the coordinates of the point at angle θ (radians) on the unit circle; exact values at multiples of π/6 and π/4; trig functions of real numbers.

topics.title: Equations of Circles
topics.summary: (x − h)² + (y − k)² = r² from the distance formula; write an equation from center and radius; find center and radius, completing the square when needed.

topics.title: Areas of Parallelograms, Trapezoids, and Kites
topics.summary: A = bh for parallelograms, ½h(b₁ + b₂) for trapezoids, ½d₁d₂ for rhombuses and kites; areas of composite figures by decomposing them.

topics.title: Prisms and Their Surface Area
topics.summary: Right and oblique prisms, parallelepipeds; rectangular solids and the diagonal √(l² + w² + h²); lateral and total surface area of prisms.

topics.title: Volumes of Prisms and Cavalieri's Principle
topics.summary: Volume postulates; V = lwh and V = Bh for prisms; Cavalieri's principle for oblique prisms; cubic units and composite solids.

topics.title: Cylinders: Surface Area and Volume
topics.summary: Right and oblique cylinders; net of a cylinder; lateral area 2πrh and total surface area; V = πr²h.

topics.title: Pyramids: Surface Area and Volume
topics.summary: Regular pyramids, slant height, lateral and total surface area; V = ⅓Bh; parallel cross sections of a pyramid; frustum of a pyramid.

topics.title: Cones: Surface Area and Volume
topics.summary: Right circular cones and slant height; lateral area πrℓ and total surface area; V = ⅓πr²h; frustum of a cone.

topics.title: Spheres: Surface Area and Volume
topics.summary: Spheres and balls, great circles, cross sections, tangent planes; S = 4πr², V = (4/3)πr³; hemispheres and composite solids.

topics.title: Perimeters and Areas of Similar Figures
topics.summary: Similar figures with scale factor k have perimeters in ratio k and areas in ratio k²; find an unknown area or scale factor. Volumes come in GE.15.9.

topics.title: Similar Solids
topics.summary: Similar solids with scale factor k have surface areas in ratio k² and volumes in ratio k³; effect of changing one or all dimensions on surface area and volume.

topics.title: Experimental and Theoretical Probability
topics.summary: Compute experimental and theoretical probabilities, complements and odds; use probability to predict and judge fairness, incl. simulations.

topics.title: Independent and Dependent Events
topics.summary: Find P(A and B) for independent events and for dependent events (without replacement), using lists, tables and tree diagrams.

topics.title: Compound Events: Mutually Exclusive and Overlapping
topics.summary: Addition rule P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A and B), mutually exclusive events, complements and Venn diagrams.

topics.title: Conditional Probability and Independence
topics.summary: P(B | A) from two-way tables, tree diagrams and the formula; the multiplication rule; test independence with P(B | A) = P(B).

topics.title: Sampling Methods and Study Design
topics.summary: Populations vs. samples; random, stratified, cluster, systematic and convenience samples; sources of bias; surveys, experiments and observational studies.

topics.title: Making Inferences from Samples
topics.summary: Estimate population proportions and means from samples, margin of error ≈ 1/√n, and compare treatments in experiments using simulation.

topics.title: Evaluating Statistical Claims
topics.summary: What a study supports: random sampling lets results generalize to the population sampled; random assignment supports cause and effect; observational data show association only.

topics.title: Units, SI Prefixes, and Unit Conversion
topics.summary: SI base units, prefixes (n, μ, m, k, M), converting with unit factors, checking an answer's units (dimensional analysis), and sensible significant figures.

topics.title: Rearranging Equations and Proportional Reasoning
topics.summary: Solve a physics equation for any variable, then reason with it: if r doubles, how does F change? Direct, inverse, square and inverse-square relationships.

topics.title: Graphs, Slope, Area, and Linearizing Data
topics.summary: Read meaning from a graph's slope and the area under it; choose axes that make data linear (e.g. y vs x², T² vs L) and get a constant from the best-fit slope.

topics.title: Experimental Design and Measurement Uncertainty
topics.summary: Independent, dependent and controlled variables; a procedure that tests a claim; measurement uncertainty and reducing it with repeated trials — the AP lab-design free-response task.

topics.title: Position, Distance, and Displacement
topics.summary: Scalars vs vectors in one dimension; a coordinate system and sign convention; distance vs displacement.

topics.title: Velocity and Speed
topics.summary: Average velocity vs average speed; instantaneous velocity; reading velocity from a position–time graph's slope.

topics.title: Acceleration
topics.summary: Average acceleration as change in velocity over time; what its sign means; speeding up vs slowing down.

topics.title: Motion Graphs: Position, Velocity, and Acceleration
topics.summary: Translate between x–t, v–t and a–t graphs using slope and area; describe motion from a graph and sketch the graph from a description.

topics.title: Constant-Acceleration Equations
topics.summary: The kinematic equations for constant acceleration, which one to use when, and solving multi-step 1-D problems.

topics.title: Free Fall
topics.summary: Motion with acceleration g only: objects dropped and thrown up, symmetry of up and down, time in the air.

topics.title: Vector Components and Vector Addition
topics.summary: Resolve a vector into x and y components with sine and cosine; add vectors by components; magnitude and direction of the resultant.

topics.title: Reference Frames and Relative Motion
topics.summary: Velocity depends on the observer; relative velocity in one dimension and simple two-dimensional cases (river crossing, wind).

topics.title: Projectile Motion: Horizontal Launch
topics.summary: Horizontal and vertical motion are independent: constant horizontal velocity, free fall vertically; time of flight and range for a horizontal launch.

topics.title: Projectile Motion: Launch at an Angle
topics.summary: Split the launch velocity into components; maximum height, time of flight, range; the 45° and complementary-angle results.

topics.title: Systems and Center of Mass
topics.summary: Choose a system; internal vs external forces; treat a system as one object at its center of mass and locate the center of mass.

topics.title: Forces and Free-Body Diagrams
topics.summary: Forces as interactions; gravity, normal, tension, friction and spring forces; drawing a correct free-body diagram and finding net force.

topics.title: Newton's Third Law
topics.summary: Force pairs: equal and opposite, on different objects, same type; why third-law pairs never cancel on one free-body diagram.

topics.title: Newton's First Law and Equilibrium
topics.summary: Inertia; zero net force means constant velocity; solving equilibrium problems, including ropes at angles.

topics.title: Newton's Second Law
topics.summary: a = F_net/m for one object: set up ΣF in each direction from the free-body diagram and solve; apparent weight in an elevator.

topics.title: Connected Objects and Systems
topics.summary: Objects joined by strings or in contact: treat the whole system, then one object; Atwood machines, blocks pushed together, a block pulled over a table edge.

topics.title: Inclined Planes
topics.summary: Tilt the axes along the slope; components of gravity mg sin θ and mg cos θ; objects sliding, held, or pushed on ramps.

topics.title: Universal Gravitation
topics.summary: F = Gm₁m₂/r²; inverse-square reasoning; gravitational force between planets, moons and objects.

topics.title: Gravitational Field and Weight
topics.summary: g = GM/r² as the gravitational field; weight as mg; how g changes with height and from planet to planet; inertial vs gravitational mass.

topics.title: Kinetic and Static Friction
topics.summary: Kinetic friction μₖN; static friction up to μₛN and why it only matches what's needed; friction on flat ground and inclines.

topics.title: Spring Forces and Hooke's Law
topics.summary: F = kΔx; spring constant from a force–stretch graph; springs in a free-body diagram.

topics.title: Uniform Circular Motion
topics.summary: Centripetal acceleration v²/r toward the center; period and speed; net inward force from real forces (no 'centrifugal force').

topics.title: Circular Motion Applications
topics.summary: Flat and banked curves, vertical circles and loops (minimum speed at the top), and circular orbits with Kepler's third law.

topics.title: Translational Kinetic Energy
topics.summary: K = ½mv²; kinetic energy as a scalar; how K scales with speed and mass.

topics.title: Work
topics.summary: Work by a constant force W = Fd cos θ; positive, negative and zero work; work as area under a force–displacement graph.

topics.title: The Work–Energy Theorem
topics.summary: Net work equals the change in kinetic energy; solving force-and-distance problems with energy instead of kinematics.

topics.title: Potential Energy
topics.summary: Potential energy of a system: gravitational mgh near Earth and −Gm₁m₂/r in general, spring ½kx²; choosing the zero level.

topics.title: Conservation of Mechanical Energy
topics.summary: In a closed system with no nonconservative work, K + U stays constant; energy bar charts; pendulums, roller coasters, springs launching objects.

topics.title: Energy with Friction and External Work
topics.summary: Work by friction and outside forces changes a system's mechanical energy; thermal energy; open vs closed systems.

topics.title: Power
topics.summary: Power as the rate of energy transfer, P = W/t and P = Fv; watts and efficiency.

topics.title: Linear Momentum
topics.summary: p = mv as a vector; momentum of a system and velocity of its center of mass.

topics.title: Impulse and Change in Momentum
topics.summary: Impulse J = FΔt = Δp; impulse as area under a force–time graph; why padding and follow-through change the force.

topics.title: Conservation of Linear Momentum
topics.summary: In an isolated system total momentum is constant; explosions and recoil; choosing the system.

topics.title: Elastic and Inelastic Collisions
topics.summary: Momentum is conserved in every collision; kinetic energy is conserved only in elastic ones; perfectly inelastic (stick-together) collisions.

topics.title: Collisions in Two Dimensions
topics.summary: Conserve momentum separately in x and y; glancing collisions.

topics.title: Rotational Kinematics
topics.summary: Angular displacement, angular velocity and angular acceleration in radians; the rotational kinematic equations.

topics.title: Connecting Linear and Rotational Motion
topics.summary: s = rθ, v = rω, aₜ = rα; points at different radii on a rotating object.

topics.title: Torque
topics.summary: τ = rF sin θ; lever arm; sign of a torque; adding torques about a chosen axis.

topics.title: Rotational Inertia
topics.summary: I = Σmr² for point masses; how mass distribution changes I; standard shapes; the parallel-axis theorem.

topics.title: Rotational Equilibrium
topics.summary: Static equilibrium needs ΣF = 0 and Στ = 0; beams, see-saws, ladders and signs; choosing the pivot.

topics.title: Newton's Second Law in Rotational Form
topics.summary: α = τ_net/I; pulleys with mass; problems that combine linear and rotational second laws.

units.title: Energy and Momentum of Rotating Systems

topics.title: Rotational Kinetic Energy
topics.summary: K = ½Iω²; total kinetic energy of objects that spin and move.

topics.title: Torque and Work
topics.summary: Work done by a torque W = τΔθ; the rotational work–energy theorem.

topics.title: Angular Momentum and Angular Impulse
topics.summary: L = Iω for a rotating object and L = mvr⊥ for a moving point; angular impulse τΔt = ΔL.

topics.title: Conservation of Angular Momentum
topics.summary: With no net external torque L is constant; spinning skaters, collisions with rotating objects.

topics.title: Rolling
topics.summary: Rolling without slipping (v = rω); kinetic energy of rolling objects; which shape wins a race down a ramp; rolling with slipping.

topics.title: Motion of Orbiting Satellites
topics.summary: Circular and elliptical orbits using conservation of energy and angular momentum; speed at different points in an orbit; escape speed.

topics.title: Simple Harmonic Motion
topics.summary: Restoring force proportional to displacement; equilibrium position, amplitude; which systems are simple harmonic.

topics.title: Period and Frequency of Oscillators
topics.summary: T = 2π√(m/k) for a mass on a spring and T = 2π√(L/g) for a pendulum; what the period does and doesn't depend on.

topics.title: Representing and Analyzing SHM
topics.summary: x(t) = A cos(2πft); position, velocity and acceleration graphs over a cycle; where speed and acceleration are greatest.

topics.title: Energy of Simple Harmonic Oscillators
topics.summary: Energy shifting between ½kx² and ½mv²; maximum speed from amplitude; energy bar charts for oscillators.

topics.title: Density and the Ideal Fluid
topics.summary: ρ = m/V; what makes a fluid ideal (incompressible, no viscosity) and why the model is used.
